comes to visit for a while. He spends hours huddled with \x01@\x13, and walks erratically over our clan lands. We shouldn’t neglect our own land by raiding during harvest time, no matter how tempting this new land seems.

Castigate the ducks for their rudeness, short stature, and foul smell. Then return home.

Remind the ducks how strong your clan is. Demand \x01@\x13 food as a token of their sincere apology.

Return home, then launch a surprise raid against the ducks.

said they had found nothing, and that the Storm Bull had grown bored and wandered off.

I can’t believe these scoundrels! They’re so — so — arrogant!

They’ll fly into a rage and kill us all!

“Defense”
We told him that defense was the most important virtue.
He thanked us for our answer. He gave us an archaic form of the Parting Words, and left.
“Honor.”
We told him that honor was the most important virtue.
“Hospitality”
We told him that hospitality was the most important virtue.
“Justice”
We told him that justice was the most important virtue.
“Obedience.”
We told him that obedience was the most important virtue.
“Provision.”
We told him that provision was the most important virtue.
Provision is the most important, for, without food, all other questions are moot.
Obedience is the most important, for without it, the other virtues cannot be enforced.
Defense is the most important, for if enemies slay us, the other virtues cannot be upheld.
Defense is the most important. If enemies slay us, the other virtues cannot be upheld.
Defense is the most important. If enemies kill us, the other virtues are worthless.
Justice is the most important. All of the written authorities say so.
Hospitality is the most important. Without it, King Heort’s Ring would never have enumerated the other virtues.
Honor is the most important. It is better to die than to lose it.
Let’s not waste time arguing over what is correct. Let’s figure out what he wants to hear.
We shall not be interrogated on our most precious beliefs by a well-dressed skink!
If we tell him the wrong thing, he will run through our market smashing things!
How can we possibly pick one of them as the most important? They’re all equal.
Hospitality is the most important virtue. Without it, no one would be able to travel, and we could entertain no guests.
Our ancestors never invited dragon-like beasts into their marketplace.
sceneR009

Someone, or something, has evaded your patrols to leave a curious gift on the doorstep of your clan hall. The gift is a basket containing large, and peculiarly shaped, eggs. The children are wonderstruck. Adults wonder whether this omen bodes good or ill.
A clutch of big, funny-shaped eggs was left on our doorstep.
Care for them until they hatch.
We decided to see what would hatch out of them, if anything.
The children were happy, and checked the eggs several times a day.
Cook them and serve to prominent carls.
We served them as the main dish at a feast honoring our carls.
The carls said they had a strong taste.
Cook them and serve to the clan ring.
Their taste was strong, and they were very filling.
Cook them and serve to top weaponthanes.
We served them as the main dish at a feast honoring our weaponthanes.
Our leading warriors said they had a strong taste, and were very filling.
Trade them away.
We decided to trade them away.
The eggs fetched a fair price.
No one wanted them.
We don’t know if these are safe to eat or not.
These could be very valuable.
They’re worth something, I imagine, but they’re still only eggs.
At best, we could get \x01@\x13 cows worth of goods for them.
The carls could use a gesture of respect about now.
Our warriors need to know that we are grateful to them.
Whoever left these meant them as a gift. We can do whatever we want with them.
If we are to understand this omen, we should look for clues as to who left them.
See the design on the basket? The same design was on the robe of Mathrania the Magnificent.
These eggs were left as children for adoption, not omelettes in waiting.
Mmm, I can taste them already.
We’re always bribing and compensating others. Let’s reserve this feast for ourselves.
Let’s leave them, and see what hatches out. Maybe we’ll get baby dragons of our very own.
It would be rude to eat these ourselves.
sceneR010

The strange eggs hatch, and stranger creatures emerge from them. They are large baby lizard-things, with a ruff of bone around their beaked faces. You can be sure that nothing this odd has ever been born in one of your barns before.
The eggs hatched, and weird little lizards came out.
Kill them immediately.
We killed them right away.
Sacrifice them to Ernalda.
We sacrificed them to Ernalda.
\x01@\x05 said the omens were favorable, and she was now closer to Ernalda.
\x01@\x05 said she could not determine whether Ernalda was pleased by the sacrifice.
Sacrifice them to Orlanth.
We sacrificed them to Orlanth.
The storm priests could not agree on the meaning of the omens.
Sacrifice them to Uralda.
We sacrificed them to Uralda.
\x01@\x14 said the omens were favorable, and she was now closer to Uralda.
\x01@\x14 said she could not determine whether Uralda was pleased by the sacrifice.
Try to raise them.
We decided to try to raise the creatures, to see what they would become.
The carls were not at all sure how they would turn out, but agreed to raise them and see.
Try to trade them to another clan.
We traded the creatures to another clan.
\x01@N was able to exchange the creatures for some trade goods.
We tried to trade them away, but in the meantime, they grew very large.
We don’t know anything about these creatures. Are they good to eat? Do they carry diseases?
Look at their teeth. They eat plants, just like cows.
Look at their shape. Those bones will grow to carry great amounts of meat.
No sane trader would accept one of these loathsome things.
These creatures are a novelty at the very least. Perhaps they are valuable.
How big do you think these get? How much pasture land will they require?
These things could be connected to the dragons. We’re in trouble.
These things could be connected to the dragons.
These creatures are called Earthshakers, and are holy to Ernalda’s sister, Maran Gor.
Whatever we do, no good will come of it.
It will be exciting and wondrous to see what these things become.
It is hard to see how we benefit either way.
Those things are revolting! What fool suggested we keep the eggs?
sceneR011

The carls grow exasperated with the big lizards. They still trample the grain once in a while, and their appetites haven’t gone down one whit. The carls say that we should make up our minds what to do with them, soon.
The carls demanded that we do something with the big lizards, which were still causing some problems.

The strange little lizards have grown up into strange, very big lizards. They’re trampling the grain, eating voraciously, and accidentally stomping the occasional chicken. No one knows what to do with them.
The strange little lizards grew up into strange big lizards. They caused many problems.
Leave them alone.
We learned how to stay out of their way, and they sort of learned how not to stomp on things, most of the time.
Sacrifice them to a god.
Which god do you sacrifice them to?
We sacrificed them.
The god-talkers said that \x01@\x07 had accepted our sacrifice.
Slaughter them for their meat.
They died like cows, but weren’t quite as tasty.
Try to train them as battle mounts.
We tried to train them as battle mounts.
The beasts seemed to slowly respond to our training.
The beasts were too wild to be tamed for war.
Try to train them as beasts of burden.
We tried to train them as beasts of burden.
Our efforts were for naught, they did not remember rewards or blows long enough to learn anything.
I don’t know whether we can train these things or not.
These creatures aren’t that much dumber than cows. I can train them as beasts of burden, I think.
These beasts aren’t that much more stupid than sheep. I’d still like to try to train them as beasts of burden.
No point in trying to trade them now, when we don’t quite know what to do with them.
No point in trying to trade them, when we still don’t quite know what to do with them or what good to say about them.
Wouldn’t it be something if we could train them as battle mounts? Imagine the effect on our foes!
I think I can train them as battle mounts. Imagine the effect on our foes as our Earthshakers thunder into sight!
I still want to try to train them as battle mounts. I want to our enemies’ faces as our Earthshakers thunder into sight!
The carls are upset with the havoc the beasts are causing.
The carls are upset, but they’ll be patient a little while longer if we can promise an eventual benefit.
The carls are at the end of their patience. We must do something, even the wrong thing.
If our resident herder won’t mention it, I will; these things are each eating as much as 3 cows. And they haven’t stopped growing!
These things are practically inhaling food. Make them earn their keep or get rid of them!
I just remembered — these Earthshaker creatures are powerful wards against Chaos. During the Darkness, they helped Maran Gor fight Wakboth the Devil.
How can you even think of getting rid of the Earthshakers, when they give protection against Chaos? A few smashed steads, and wagonloads of grain, is a small price for this blessing.
They’re kin to dragons, I tell you, dragons! And we all know what kind of trouble that means!
Don’t forget that there’s probably some kind of dragon connection to all of this.
At least some people in this clan see the trouble these dragon-kin bring us!
Whatever we do with them, make sure we don’t do something that would offend the dragonewts.
I knew it. We should have killed the things as soon as they popped out of their eggs.
I knew we shouldn’t have let those things run around loose.
Big horns, big fun!
If we eat them, our fertility problems will be solved. Forever.
I’ll have them rolling over and begging for scraps in no time.
Earth cows!
The menfolk will try to turn the Earthshakers into weapons, but they belong to Ernalda’s sister, and should be used in planting.
To ride one of these powerful beasts — what a thrill that would be!
“A visitor must not outstay his welcome.”
“Don’t empty your host’s larder when you go to visit.”
\x02\x03Genevra/Asandra/Chella\x02

The big lizards we raised haven’t been seen for the last few days. We were just getting to used to them, too! One of our carls, \x01@\x07, reported that she last saw them slowly walking, single file, in the direction of Kero Fin. The children will miss them, but the carls are relieved that the creatures, along with their enormous appetites, are gone.
sceneR012
A trio of strange beings has eluded your patrols. These lizard-men are probably the dragonewts you’ve heard legends about. For twelve hours they have been enacting a mysterious ritual on your lands.
A trio of dragonewts has eluded your patrols. For twelve hours they have been enacting a mysterious ritual on your lands.
Dragonewts eluded our patrols, and did strange things on our land.
Clear the area until they leave.
We avoided them.
Conduct a ritual to counter their magic.
We conducted a ritual in hopes of defusing whatever dragon magic they were brewing.
Our god-talkers said that their ritual had thwarted the dragonewts.
Our god-talkers said that their ritual had probably thwarted the dragonewts.
Try to communicate with them.
We tried to communicate with them.
The dragonewts glanced at us briefly, then went back to their ritual. Two hours later, they left our lands.
Our warriors attacked them.
When struck with our swords, they hissed ferociously. Our stream ran thick with their green blood.
Watch them until they leave.
The ritual continued for two hours. Then, as abruptly as they came, they left.
This is all that I Saw. Or rather, there were seven different things that happened \x02\x02afterwards/next\x02. Which \x02\x02isn’t very useful/is not helpful\x02.
Perhaps we can try to communicate with them.
Dragonewts are trouble. Very serious trouble.
Dragonewts are very strange indeed. No one really understands why they do certain things.
What is everyone afraid of? It’s not like they’re broos, for Urox’s sake.
Run and hide. We must run and hide. Run. And Hide.
By Maran Gor’s trembling thighs, there shall be no overgrown salamanders cavorting about beside our creek bed!
Surely we have offended the gods, to bring such a terrible omen down on our heads.
Please take me off the ring. I’m not up to dealing with dragonewts.
We could bribe them… if we could figure out what a dragonewt wants.
“When in the fields, a man should never move an inch from his weapons.”
These aren’t the toughest dragonewts. These are the weakest ones.
Hey! They’re stealing our honey!
Music is the universal language. I will go sing to them, and learn why they are here.
Crested snakes steal flower’s gold.
Dragon’s little brothers dance foot-wet with striped warriors.
This is like the old stories from the Empire of Wyrm’s Friends!
Let’s see how well they fight.
I think this is wonderful. Good things are sure to follow.
sceneR013

Illator, a noble of Tarsh, comes to visit you. He tells you of his land. Tarsh is a kingdom to the northwest. Its people are Orlanthi who, like you, follow the laws of King Heort. They are from another part of the world, though, and may do things very differently from you. Once Illator has given you his news, he has an offer. Tarsh’s king, Arim, is waging war against the empire to his north, called the Lunar Empire. Illator wants to hire some of your weaponthanes as mercenaries for a several-season military campaign. “There will be much loot,” he says. “Many, many cows, you will gain.”
We were approached by Illator, a noble of Tarsh. He sought mercenaries for a northern war.
Decline his offer.
We declined his offer.
Do you…
Simply, but politely, decline?
Send a gift to the Tarshite king?
However, we sent a gift to the Tarshite king.
Ask Illator not to bother you again?
Further, we told Illator never to darken our door again.
Send a quarter of your weaponthanes.
Do you send your war leader \x01@\x17 to lead the weaponthanes?
We sent \x01@\x17 and a quarter of our weaponthanes north to help King Arim.
We sent a quarter of our weaponthanes north to help King Arim.
Send a token force.
We sent \x01@\x17 and a token force north to help King Arim.
We sent a token force north to help King Arim.
Send half of your weaponthanes.
We sent \x01@\x17 and half of our weaponthanes north to help King Arim.
We sent half of our weaponthanes north to help King Arim.
Send three-quarters of your weaponthanes.
We sent \x01@\x17 and three-quarters of our weaponthanes north to help King Arim.
We sent three-quarters of our weaponthanes north to help King Arim.
And how exactly are they going to drive “many, many cows” all the way down from the Lunar Empire?
The greater the force we send, the greater the loot we will gain.
No good outcome is ever guaranteed in war. We must balance the chance for great gain with the great risk of sending many warriors.
The greater the force we send, the greater the risk we take.
We’re too vulnerable to be selling our swords.
His foe is the empire of the same red moon that gave our priests headaches before the Pharaoh came.
If their enemy is Chaotic, then we should offer to fight for free!\t\t
We can loyally guard the stead while the other warriors go off to fight.
“It is good to be wise, but not so wise that you acutely feel the misfortunes of the world.”
This reminds me of, there was a time that, something is making me think, I’m sorry, it’s just on the tip of my tongue…
The war will unfold as it is destined to unfold, no matter how many warriors we send.
Finally, a chance to prove ourselves in a genuine war!
sceneR014

Clearly, your neighbors have discovered that you’ve sent many of your warriors off to war. A team of ducks, taking advantage of your temporary weakness, has stolen cows from your herd over a period of several nights.
When our warriors were serving as mercenaries up north, ducks came and stole from our herds.
Demand satisfaction from the duck chieftain.
We demanded satisfaction from the duck chieftain.
\x01@\x03, the duck chieftain, agreed that we had been wronged. He ordered the thieves to return the stolen cattle, and pay compensation to boot.
\x01@\x03, the duck chieftain, agreed that we had been wronged, but said that the thieves were outlaws from his clan. Without admitting fault, he gave us a cow as “a token of friendship.”

\x01@\x03, the duck chieftain, agreed that we had been wronged, but said that the thieves were outlaws from his clan. “We are as anxious to catch them as you,” he said, “but they are like feathers on the wind.”
Free the ducks from their obligation to you if they deal with this.
We approached the duck chieftain, \x01@\x03, and offered to end their tribute to us, if he would reign in the Duck cattle thieves. He agreed, and, to show good faith, compensated our losses.
Persuade the carls that any losses now will be offset by loot from the war.
They replied that they’d been blinded by their own loss, and had lost sight of the clan as a whole.
Promise the carls you’ll raid the ducks when the warriors get back.
We promised the carls that we would raid the ducks when the warriors returned.
They looked forward to joining the raiding party, once the weaponthanes returned from the war in the north.
Send a war party to frighten the rustlers.
We sent a party to find and frighten the thieves.
The guilty ducks could not be found.
Relentlessly did we track them. Remorselessly did we strike fear into their tiny hearts.
Our reservists tracked them relentlessly, but were handed a stinging defeat by the tricky thieves.
Send a war party to kill the rustlers.
We sent a party to find and slay the thieves.
Relentlessly did we track them. Remorselessly did we strike them down.
It is never a good time to be robbed, but our herds are large, so things could be worse.
We cannot stand for this. Our herds are dwindling, and every loss is a serious one.
It is no use negotiating with thieves. But the duck chieftain may have something to offer us.
We could gain much if we released the ducks from their tribute obligations.
Many of our best men are away at the war. Our reserves may have trouble even with a few ducks.
Our best men are away at the war. Our reserves might well get themselves killed, even by ducks.
The carls are discontented now, but they’ve forgotten how many cows Illator has promised us.
It is good to be robbed now and then. It teaches humility.
We must strike forcefully against the ducks! We must show that we can protect the hearth while the warriors are off questing.
We should remind the duck chieftain just how tasty he would be if boiled with cabbages and onions.
Live by the sword, die by the sword.
We’ve really made fools of ourselves now. The carls will throw us all off the ring if we don’t please them.
I told you that enemies would attack us if we sent too many warriors away.
This is a good chance to show our generosity.

The warriors are back from the campaign against the Lunars. Excitedly, they tell the tale of fighting for clever King Arim, whose magical twin children dropped a range of hills on the enemy. Proudly, they tell of their own valiant exploits in battle, and show off their loot.

The warriors returned from the campaign against the northern empire. There, they saw King Arim’s magical twins drop a range of hills on the Chaotic foe. They gathered goodly loot, and brought it back to us.

The warriors are back from the campaign against the Lunars. Wearily, they tell how they fought for the clever but capricious King Arim. Dejectedly, they tell of their own terrible fate, cut off by Lunar troops and forced to rout through a wall of sorcerous fire. Arim won the battle, but used our warriors as game pieces.
Only some of our warriors returned from the campaign against the northern empire. The clever but capricious King Arim won the battle, but used us as game pieces.
Give some of the warriors’ loot to the carls.
Because all had sacrificed, all were rewarded with loot from the war.
The carls were pleased that their sacrifices had not gone unrewarded, but some of the warriors cast lingering looks at the loot they’d brought back.
Launch a raid against the ducks.
In celebration of our victory, we attacked the ducks.
Recruit additional warriors.
We thought it a good time to seek permanent reinforcements.
We found warriors eager to join the triumphant warriors of the Battle of Falling Hills.
Warriors refused to join us, saying that our forces were destroyed in a great victory for the Orlanthi. They said we were unlucky.
Our recruiting efforts failed.
Reward the warriors with a feast.
With a feast, we celebrated the valor of our warriors.
Our warriors resigned themselves to the fickleness of luck in war. Our carls shared their burdens, and urged them to find cheer in simple things.
Our warriors composed great poems celebrating their deeds. Our carls toasted them, and observed that no one would dare steal from us now.
Sacrifice to the war gods.
To cleanse ourselves of our bad luck, we sacrificed to Orlanth and other war gods.
To show thanks for our good luck, we sacrificed to Orlanth and other war gods.
The priests said the omens were good.
The priests were troubled; they couldn’t read the omens.
So where are all those cows Illator promised us?
War is a cruel mistress; our side won, but our forces lost.
We should trust more in the abilities of our fighting force.
War is a cruel mistress; our side won, but our warriors suffered. We must work to restore their confidence.
Illator may be from a foreign land, but he is still an Orlanthi. I trust his oaths to pay us.
King Arim has accomplished much. Perhaps we in Dragon Pass should have a king, too…
We owe our luck to the gods. We must repay them.
War gods respect the victorious. They are unlikely to smile on us now.
It would be foolish to send our warriors off so soon, especially since it’s planting time.
It would be foolish to send our warriors off so soon, especially since it’s harvest time.
While the warriors have been off fighting, the carls have been accumulating resentments. They deserve our attention.
Shame wears us like a dirty cloak. We must smash someone, anyone, to regain our lost reputation.
Now that our warriors know of Tarsh, we should launch our own raid!
I’m sure we haven’t seen the last of Illator.
The battlefield is the greatest trickster of all.
We share the ultimate responsibility for this disaster. We should all resign.
King Arim’s hallowed victory puts us all to shame.
For mighty warriors, these fellows are easily thrown into a sulk.
We’re in for much strutting and posing in the weeks ahead.
The course of the battle was preordained. Our role in it was too insignificant to predict one way or the other.
The beastfolk are our ancient enemies. It’s always a good time to raid the ducks.
sceneR016

The Tarshite noble Illator is back, bearing payment for your contribution to the Battle of Falling Hills. Unfortunately, he deceived you! Instead of the cows he promised, he’s brought chest after chest of small silver coins bearing the face of a beardless tyrant.
Many members of the clan look crestfallen; they distinctly remember his promise to give us cows.
Illator of Tarsh came to pay us for our warriors’ mercenary services, but tried to get us to take foreign coins instead of the cows he promised.
Grudgingly accept the wealth.
With great reluctance, we took his coins.
Nobody wanted to give back the coins, but the people still felt cheated. The warriors would have preferred arm rings or torcs, and the herders had clearly been already counting the promised cows.
Hold Illator hostage; have his men get the cows.
We held Illator hostage, and sent his men to get the cows we were owed.
Illator said, “You may be brave in battle, but you are fools in council.” We waited for his king to make good on his promise.
Kill Illator and send his head back to King Arim.
To show King Arim that we were no fools to be swindled, we sent him his thane’s head in a box. To show him proper respect, it was a very pretty box.
Ask him to instead sacrifice to strengthen your clan magic.
He sacrificed to the gods on our behalf, and the dispute between us was resolved.
Send Illator back to Tarsh to get cows.
Illator says that this would be very difficult, and he will take no responsibility for cows that die on the long trip down.
Do you still insist on cows?
We insisted that Illator bring us cows, as he’d promised. He returned to Tarsh to do so.
Illator returned to Tarsh. Someone thought he heard Illator call us fools, but it was hard to be certain, given his accent.
Illator was glad we’d decided to be reasonable after all.
Cows. Illator promised us cows. So cows we must get.
Only effete, prancing minstrels value these coins.
We could at least melt down the silver from these coins.
Coins are an odd way to work silver, but they are valuable as trade goods, at least.
These coins are valuable despite their origin, and they are offering a staggering number of them. Take the coins!
A promise is a promise.
Normally, we’d be able to request that his clan help us in battle, but Tarsh is too distant to arrange that. But they can supply magic we can use in a fight.
He’s trying to steal from us, and he’s a foreigner. The law allows us to harshly punish him.
We are entitled to stick to the strict letter of the agreement.
Although the Tarshites are foreigners, they are also Orlanthi. Precedent suggests we give them the benefit of the doubt.
Arim is far away, but he is a great king. He won’t take kindly to our killing Illator or taking him hostage.
Orlanth saw Ernalda prisoner in the Emperor’s palace. He stormed the palace, killing all defenders.
Tell Illator that our only use for his precious coins is to stick them on his cold, dead eyes.
We have fought beside the Tarshites. Let us now see what it is like to fight against them.
They are deceivers. Worse than thieves. Cows they promised, and cows they shall give.
Take the coins. As each is worth little, it will not pain us to spend them.
We may have misunderstood Illator when he made his promise — he certainly doesn’t speak our language well.
Honor is one of the most important virtues. We should give Illator the chance to make good on his word.
Chiefs are ring-givers, not coin-strewers!
I hate to bring it up, but Illator did promise us cows. Not small bits of silver.
Is this some odd magic, all those heads of a foreign tyrant?
sceneR017

Normally, good Orlanthi try to avoid looking at the Chaotic red moon that hangs in the northern sky. But one night your holy people notice that great, black scars have appeared on its surface. This means something of great import, surely.
Our holy people saw great scars appear on the surface of the Chaotic red moon.
Do nothing; the moon is not our concern.
Concerned, we increased our patrols.
The weaponthanes kept one eye on the baleful moon and one eye out for other danger.
Sacrifice to Urox, foe of Chaos.
Because the moon is of Chaos, we sacrificed to Urox, foe of Chaos.
Our god-talkers said they heard the bellowing of a bull, and that our lands would be protected against Chaos.
The god-talkers could not read the omens.
Use magical divination to understand what is happening.
\x01@\r conducted a divination ritual to understand what was happening.
\x01@\r looked at the entrails of a sheep, and saw in them the image of a great and terrible horseman. This horseman had ridden to the moon, where he was destroying the Lunar servants of Chaos.
\x01@\r looked at the entrails of a sheep, and saw that the Lunars were readying their forces on the moon to launch an assault against the peoples of Dragon Pass.
Warn nearby clans of supernatural menace.
We warned our neighbors of the possibility of supernatural trouble. It turned out that they had seen the scars, too, though no one could agree on what they meant.
The scars mean that our cow’s milk is going to dry up.
This is frightening, but perhaps it gives us a chance to patch up relations with our neighbors.
This is a bad omen for any raids conducted at night.
This means that our wheat will be afflicted with a poisonous blight.
I hear Urox stomping in the night, asking to be unleashed against the enemy.
The moon is an invader, its light is not pure.
Those are wounds.
I can perform a divination ritual to perhaps explain this strange occurrence.
The wild old world does not always revolve around our clan.
The moon is a thing of Chaos. If it is scarred, that means Chaos has lost a great battle.
What goes up, must come down.
Let us sacrifice every cow we can spare to Urox, foe of Chaos.
If we continue our sacrifices to Orlanth, perhaps the moon will come down!
This has nothing to do with us.
Scars on the moon! I never promised you I could help you with scars on the moon when I agreed to join the ring!
I don’t think this is bad.
I feel sick. Don’t the rest of you feel sick, too?
The Lunar Empire is being punished for its war-like ways. The scars are an omen of peace.
Only the gods can protect us from such a frightening omen.
We should make sure other clans recognize this danger.
The world is connected in strange ways. We need to be careful.
There’s a proverb about the moon that seems appropriate, but I can’t quite remember it.
So?
I knew this was going to be a year for great omens.
The moon has been attacked. It is a good omen for all attackers. Let’s launch a raid soon.
sceneR018

Foreigners are found in one of the holy sheds where women’s magic is practiced. This is double sacrilege. Not only are these people so strange to you that you don’t even know where they’re from, but there are men among them! No men are ever permitted to step inside one of these sheds. The priestesses must conduct a ritual of purification, but even so, your clan fertility may be seriously disrupted.
Strange foreigners were found defiling one of Ernalda’s holy sheds. Our women conducted a ritual of purification.
We showed mercy and merely drove them off.
The women were too busy purifying the holy sheds to protest the ring’s decision until the foreigners had fled. Some people still can’t believe we let them live.
Force them into thralldom.
We forced them into thralldom.

They begged for better treatment, saying that they were refugees from the Lunar Empire. They said their homeland had been attacked by a barbarian horseman called Sheng Seleris, and that war had torn out the Empire’s heart. They were on the run from an unjust usurper, just as we were when we fled Heortland. We told them they were lucky to be alive.
Kill the men; enslave the women.
We killed the men and enslaved the women.

They begged for better treatment, saying that they were refugees from the Lunar Empire. They said their homeland had been attacked by a barbarian horseman called Sheng Seleris, and that war had torn out the Empire’s heart. They were on the run from an unjust usurper, just as we were when we fled Heortland. We told them they should be grateful we weren’t killing their women, too.
Of course, we killed the defilers.
The people were glad that we’d killed the defilers.
Ask them who they are, then kill them.

The defilers said they were refugees from the Lunar Empire. They said their homeland had been attacked by a barbarian horseman called Sheng Seleris, and that war had torn out the Empire’s heart. “Life here could be better. We both have crafts to trade, young people to marry, and other enemies to fight. Why are we wasting time fighting each other, when we have so many other, more profitable, things to do?”

“Life here is quite workable. There are enough Orlanthi to trade with, and plenty of good land for everyone to farm. Why not come to a responsible agreement and end our futile fight? Shall we gladden the hearts of our other enemies by fighting each other, instead of shedding their blood?”
“We accept your offer of peace! Let us feast!”

Perhaps we can forge a new tribe with them, now that they see what strong tribe-mates we’d make.

Mad-Blood \x01@p said that it was bad to rely on others for food.

The tribal temple must house the most impressive regalia in all of Dragon Pass.
They are weak. We should be fighting them, not begging them to join us.
We can trust them.
Our clans will get along well in a tribe.

The \x01@! clan is known for its long-range planning, and for a tavern it maintains as part of its market. “The daughters of your thanes will be in good hands.”

We have been enemies until now. But maybe that can change.

Vingan queens?
The \x01@! warriors will be welcome here.

Could work.

We negotiated with Clan \x01@!, the first clan to settle in our immediate area, to see if we could bring them into our tribe.

“It is our right, as one of the first clans to defeat the menace of the crossline, to take the forefront at this confederation moot. We shall be there.”

If they’re in a tribe with us, they won’t be allowed to steal our cows.

Demand their blessings, then offer one seat and propitiate the cross spirit. If that doesn’t work, then promise them their war.
Demand their blessings, then offer two seats and propitiate the cross spirit. If that doesn’t work, then promise them their war.
Demand their blessings, then offer three seats and propitiate the cross spirit. If that doesn’t work, then promise them their war.

I don’t know if we can bargain with a hostile clan, but it’s worth a try. Offer two seats, demand their blessings, and propitiate the spirit. If that doesn’t work, then promise them their war.
I don’t know if we can bargain with a hostile clan, but it’s worth a try. Offer three seats, demand their blessings, and propitiate the spirit. If that doesn’t work, then promise them their war.

The other clans will balk if we promise too much.

They are worthy of a seat or even two, but the other clans will balk if we promise them more.
All they want is to rub our noses in their superiority.
They think they’re better than us. We’ll have to make many concessions if we continue negotiating, but I don’t think it’s worth it.
They used up all their magic coming through the crossline. Their blessings are worthless.
Their blessings would be powerful.

What are these dried-up old fools going to do to us? Tremble so heartily that we take pity on them?
If only we could turn their hatred against the forest folk.
What could be more thrilling than a war against the beastfolk?
They were first here. We are part of their fate, nothing more.
Even if we get them into our tribe, how do we know they won’t just continue the feud?
No organization, not even a tribe, can prevent Orlanthi from avenging their kin.
Any organization, even a tribe, can agree to do something stupid — like fight the Beastfolk.
We can meet in Lhankor Mhy’s weather at the moot, rather than Humakt’s weather on the field.
If we give them seats on the council, they will support us when the time comes to pick a king.
If we can end the feud, we look like kings. Let’s offer representation on the king’s council.
They took one of the dragonewt’s crosses! They are too brave, or crazy. We should have nothing to do with them!
If we can get them into our tribe, they will start attending our temples.
At last! A war worthy of our honor!

They said it would be good to worry only about foreign enemies, and not about trouble from other Orlanthi. They agreed to help make Saraska’s kingdom.

They spit and rattled their swords. They said that if they could not be raided by their neighbors, that also meant they could not raid their neighbors. “The first would be good, but the second would be bad,” they said. They refused to help make Saraska’s kingdom.
“Saraska is a great leader.”
We told them, “Saraska is a great leader.”
They said that her royal attributes were obvious, and that they would be pleased to bow down to her. They agreed to help make a kingdom for her.

They scoffed and jeered, saying, “We have not seen any evidence of Saraska’s so-called great qualities. We hear a lot of hot wind blowing by, but where is the action?” They refused to make a kingdom for her.
“Saraska’s magic will carry us all to greatness.”
We told them, “Saraska’s magic will carry us all to greatness.”
They said that they had already heard stories of the great magic that surrounded Saraska, and knew that the prophecies commanded them to build a kingdom for her.

They said that they did not wish to seem impious, but they had seen no evidence of Saraska’s magic. Before we could say anything, Saraska stepped forward and said, “Proof I am prepared to offer,” Saraska said, “For the gods themselves support my claims.” She strode confidently outside the tribal hall. It had been a clear day, but now glorious dark clouds rolled up. All murmured that this was a good omen indeed, that she had the favor of Orlanth. “Orlanth, I call on you to recognize my right to rule! Ernalda, I call on you to recognize my bounty and goodness! Lhankor Mhy, I call on you to recognize my love for the law!”

“With three tribes, we can make a kingdom,” Saraska said. “The others will come after I am crowned. They will come willingly, or by force if need be. Now I must prepare myself for the rites, to create a great Crown Test and pass it.”

Rejoin.

Stay independent.

Rejoining the tribe will make trade so much easier.
We are bound by our decision if we want to save face.
Their admission of error is enough welcome back for us.
Do we want to rejoin a tribe that cannot listen to wise counsel?
Our clan is better off in a tribe that can recognize and correct its lapses of judgment.
Her magic was not as strong as everyone thought.
I knew her magic was not as strong as she said. But ours will be better if we are part of a tribe.

We must warn our old tribe; they were our friends, and we should not shed their blood.

In the First Age, the Northern Horse People stood against the way Orlanth wanted things. The Heortlings made war on them.
We will prove ourselves on the field of battle, and all of our weapons will be given legendary names!
Threaten our old tribe.

sceneR234
It is time to fight for Saraska’s kingdom. Among the other clans of your tribe, you take the field against the \x01Á.
We attacked the \x01Á, in the name of Saraska’s new kingdom.

\x01Á surprises you with an attack on your tribal hall. The object of their attack is clearly Saraska; despite the prophecies, they want to destroy her kingdom before it is born. The clans of your tribe rush to meet them on the battlefield. There is no time for an orderly plan of battle.
The \x01Á attacked us, seeking to destroy Saraska’s new kingdom before its birth.
Fight as honor demands, no less and no more.
We fought no less than, and no more than, honor demanded.

Our warriors fought well, taking opportunities to press ahead when they came, and retreating when necessary. They felled a number of our foes, and won the respect of our fellows without seeking undue risks.

Our warriors fought well, taking opportunities to press ahead when they came, and retreating when necessary. Unfortunately, many of them were trapped in a ravine, and some were slain. Others were wounded. Such are the fortunes of war.
We decided that it was best to risk as little as possible in this war.

We feinted and evaded. We made warlike noises. We retreated before it was necessary, and avoided risky attacks, no matter how tempting they seemed. Some of the other warriors spoke ill of us, but we started the battle as we ended it — with no warriors dead, and none badly wounded.

We feinted and evaded, making warlike noises but retreating before it was necessary. We avoided risky attacks, no matter how tempting. Still, the ferocious weaponthanes of the \x01@! clan trapped some of our fighters in a ravine, and slew them.
Fight without quarter.
We fought without quarter.
Our warriors were second to none in ferocity and bravery. We felled many of our foes. We showed no mercy, and those of us who fell received none. We drew blood, and we shed blood.

Our warriors charged into the fray, shouting to the war gods and warning their foes that they would receive no mercy. Courage was with them that day, but luck was not. Warrior after warrior fell beneath the blades of our foes. Many died. Many more were wounded.
Argue for surrender.
We argued for surrender.
Saraska cursed us as cowards. She spurred her horse onwards and into the battle. The others of our tribe followed her. Honor gave us no choice but to follow.
Sacrifice to the war gods before battle begins.
Before we did so, we sacrificed to the gods.
The god-talkers said that the omens were bad. The gods did not favor Saraska.
The god-talkers said that omens were unclear.
The gods will understand that we cannot afford to sacrifice to them.
If ever an occasion demanded a generous sacrifice, it is this one.
What would we rather see punctured — our pride, or our flesh?
Saraska is in no mood to surrender.
Saraska is in no mood to surrender. If she rides into battle, the others will follow.
We are not a war clan. We do not kill things, we grow things.
Fight without quarter!
The greater risks we take, the greater honor we gain. If we win, that is. If we lose, we will suffer more.
The others will admire us if we fight without quarter, and will jeer at us if we fight cautiously.
It is a good time to sacrifice to the gods.
It is a bad time to sacrifice to the gods.
Are we sure that the gods favor Saraska?
There is no help for it. The crops will suffer from war.
Any fight worth fighting is worth fighting to the death.
They will rue the day they aligned themselves against Saraska!
Shed as little blood as possible.
The sky is shot with russet clouds, as it was the day Tragic King Errarth was slain.
O woe, what an awful day!
By Orlanth’s klanth, it could not be a better day!
I knew it would come to this.
sceneR235

The time has come for Saraska to undergo the Crown Test. She has created a set of magical rites that combine elements from the kingship rites of each tribe, including yours. It is a time of celebration, for this event will be remembered for all of history. There is also a sense of apprehension, for the Crown Test is sometimes dangerous, and, even though the prophecies are said to foreordain her success, some can’t help but worry about Saraska.
The time came for Saraska’s Crown Test.
What is the total value of the gifts and food you give away?
The thanes accused us of being opportunists and schemers.
Our people celebrated throughout the day. Many toasts were made in honor of the ring.
The people were cheerless, and drank so little that the ring was saddened.
Lend your magic to aid Saraska.
We decided to lend our magic to aid Saraska.
Sacrifice to the gods in honor of Saraska.
Secretly use your magic to hinder Saraska.
The people are in a good mood. There is no need to cheer them up.
The people are in a bad mood. They could use some cheering up.
The warriors are in good spirits. They don’t need encouragement to drink and celebrate.
The warriors are dispirited. We should celebrate with them, and do them honor.
We are already well respected in Dragon Pass, and can turn our thoughts to other matters.
Our name is reviled throughout Dragon Pass. We must repair our tattered reputation.
If prophecy dictates that Saraska will be queen, we needn’t use up our clan magic to support her. She will pass the Crown Test.
We can sacrifice to the gods, gaining both the normal benefits of sacrifices, and the respect of our tribe-mates.
When he took the throne, Good King Oskul said, “My Crown Test was hunting and killing Bad King Urgrain.”
If we improve our relations with others, our trade opportunities will increase.
Good relations mean that our legal claims will be honestly entertained.
Let’s turn our magic against her, and see if those prophecies are really true.
After she passes the Crown Test, Saraska will lead the new kingdom against the loathsome elves.
How can anyone even suggest that we would use bad magic against Saraska? She would pass the Crown Test, and then destroy us!
After she passes the Crown Test, Saraska will lead us to a new era of healing and compassion.
After she passes the Crown Test, Saraska will announce a great new temple building campaign.
After she passes the Crown Test, Saraska will forge a grand alliance with the dragonewts.
Something bad is going to happen.

\x01@\x01 is sent by his fellow warriors to speak to the ring. They want to quit the tribe. “We joined the tribe so that we would be strong in battle and prosperous in peace. Yet the tribe has brought us nothing but dishonor. We have tasted bitter defeat, and seen gross misrule. It is better to face the dangers of Dragon Pass as an independent clan than to heap shame upon the traditions of our ancestors.”
The warriors said that the tribe had brought us nothing but shame, and that we should leave it.
Compose a poem detailing the successes of the tribe.
We composed a poem detailing the successes of the tribe.

Our poem reminded them of the past glories of the tribe, and the great future that lay ahead of it. \x01@\x01 withdrew his complaint, and said that we had honored the warriors by giving them a fair hearing.
“\x01@N’s kennings are usually better, \x04 choice of words bolder,” \x01@\x01 said. “Accept it; the tribe is weak inspiration for poetry because the tribe is weak. We must quit the tribe.”
The warriors cheered our decision.
Tell other chieftains that your warriors are dissatisfied.
We told the other chieftains that our warriors were dissatisfied.
To prove our worth to them, they gave us gifts.

When the warriors saw these gifts, they were chastened. “Our words were over-hasty,” \x01@\x01 said. “The generosity of the other chieftains shows that there is much honor in our tribe, and that we were wrong to say we should quit.”

When the warriors saw these gifts, they were thoughtful. “The other chieftains want us to stay, but are careful not to strain themselves lifting goods onto the gifting-cart. We wait and see if they better deserve our comradeship in the future.”
The other chieftains told us that we should better discipline our warriors. “You should give them more gifts, so that they do not bother you with foolish complaints.”
“Things will get better.”
We told them that things would get better.
The warriors were convinced by our argument. \x01@\x01 withdrew his complaint, saying that they would give the tribe another chance to prove its worth to us.
“Your arguments are weak,” \x01@\x01 said. “Not because you argue poorly, but because the tribe itself is weak. You yourselves must realize that there is no good choice but to quit.”
Without a tribe, our cattle will be more vulnerable to raiding.
Do what the warriors say.
The warriors are coming to us before it is too late. We can still fix things.
The warriors are very dissatisfied. Talk will not fix things. Only a sign of generosity from the tribe will do.
A show of generosity will appease the warriors.
An argument is quickly forgotten, but a good poem is remembered forever.
When all the world was gone, and every man was alone, Heort went out upon the world.
There is no surer token of reconciliation than a generous gift.
Sever our ties with this dishonorable tribe.
We never should have joined a tribe in the first place.
If we quit the tribe, our old tribe-mates will attack us!
We cannot give up now, and throw away everything we’ve built.
We’ve been carrying this woebegone collection of clans since the day we joined!
sceneR237

War is inevitable. The upheavals caused by Saraska’s claims will not end until she and her allies are defeated on the battlefield. Or so you tell your warriors as you prepare to attack. Among the other clans of your tribe, you take the field against the \x01Á.
We attacked the \x01Á, to put to an end the dangerous plans of the false leader, Saraska.
The \x01Á attacked us, in support of Saraska’s new kingdom.

Our warriors fought well, taking opportunities to press ahead when they came, and retreating when necessary. They felled a number of our foes, and won the respect of our fellows without taking undue risks.

Our warriors fought well, taking opportunities to press ahead when they came, and retreating when necessary. Unfortunately, many of them were boxed in by cruel Saraska’s warriors, and were hacked down. Some were slain; others were wounded.

We feinted and evaded. We made warlike noises. We retreated before it was necessary, and avoided risky attacks, no matter how tempting they seemed. Some of the other warriors spoke ill of us, but we started the battle as we ended it — with no warriors dead, and none seriously wounded.

We feinted and evaded, making warlike noises. We retreated before it was necessary, and avoided risky attacks, no matter how tempting. Still, the ferocious weaponthanes of the \x01@! clan trapped some of our fighters in a gully, and slew them. Others were wounded.
Our warriors were second to none in ferocity and bravery. We felled many of our foes. We showed no mercy, and those of us who fell received none. We drew blood, and we shed it.

The other clans agreed that this was the best option. We swore to support Saraska and help make her kingdom. She accepted our pledge of fealty, and said she would go to seek another tribe to join with us.
The other clans refused to surrender. They promised to fight Saraska, who sought to steal their freedom from them. Honor gave us no choice but to fight with the rest of our tribe.
The god-talkers said that the omens were good. The gods did not favor Saraska after all.
The god-talkers said that omens were bad. The gods surely favored Saraska.
If Saraska is false, there is no need to sacrifice to assure her doom. If she is true, no sacrifice will aid us.
Saraska’s fate may be in the hands of the gods, but if sacrifice will protect our warriors, we should do it.
The others will mock us if we suggest surrender now.
The others respect us. They will consider surrender if we advise it.
They will rue the day they aligned themselves with Saraska!
When Lokamayadon usurped the rightful worship of Orlanth, everything went bad. But Harmast Barefoot risked all to quest for the hero Arkat, who destroyed the usurper.
Saraska is the worst of tyrants. The only way to assure her death is to fight without quarter.
We don’t want to be mocked by others. Then again, we don’t want to die in droves, either.
There is a time to fight, that time is now. Even peace clans must be ready to defend themselves with honor!
I feel the wrath of Orlanth singing in my blood!
It is time to rid the world of this pest.
Warriors of our clan were present when Saraska was brought down to meet her inevitable fate.
sceneR238

Near death, the hero Derik Furman is borne into your clan hall. “He slew Jaldon Goldentooth, the great Praxian incarnation of death, and buried him beneath a cairn of skulls. But the blows Jaldon dealt to him took their toll soon after he did so, and Derik has not regained consciousness since. Since you were not willing to aid him in his fight, we ask that you help him now.”

Near death, the hero Derik Furman is borne into your clan hall. “He slew Jaldon Goldentooth, the great Praxian incarnation of death, and buried him beneath a cairn of skulls. But the blows Jaldon dealt to him took their toll soon after he did so, and Derik has not regained consciousness since.”
Derik Furman’s warriors brought him into our clan hall, gravely wounded. He had slain Jaldon Goldentooth.
The mercenaries your gifts helped hire were instrumental in defeating Jaldon’s Praxian raiders.
The warriors you sent were instrumental in defeating Jaldon’s Praxian raiders.
All of them were slain.
Half of them were slain. The others were wounded.
A third of them were slain. The others were wounded. They considered themselves lucky to be back at all
A quarter of them were slain. The others were wounded. They considered themselves lucky to be back.
They all returned, but each of them had suffered serious wounds.
The magic you lent them was instrumental in defeating Jaldon’s nomad shamans.
Send for Chalana Arroy priestesses to heal Derik.
We sent for Chalana Arroy priestesses to heal Derik.

There were no priestesses to be found; Jaldon’s raids had wounded hundreds of people, so no healers could be spared for the one who had laid him to rest. Derik remained unconscious for close to a season.

Priestesses were hard to find; Jaldon’s raids had wounded hundreds of people, so they were in great demand. But we found one healer willing to treat the one who had laid death’s champion to rest. Derik regained consciousness a few days after the treatment. Within a week, he was able to stand. Within two weeks, he was able to spar with his warrior companions.
Tell Derik’s followers to take him elsewhere.
We told Derik’s followers to take him elsewhere.
They did so, although it made them unhappy. Our warriors complained that we had no honor.
Tend to Derik as he recovers.
We tended to him as he recovered. He remained unconscious for close to a season.
Tend to Derik; allow his followers to stay here until he recovers.
We tended to Derik, and allowed his followers to stay until he recovered.
Derik remained unconscious for close to a season. During that time, his many followers ate heartily.
Try to magically heal Derik.
We tried to magically heal Derik.
His condition showed no improvement. He remained unconscious for close to a season.
He regained consciousness a few days later. Within a week, he was able to stand. Within two weeks, he was able to spar with his warrior companions.
The carls are afraid that Derik’s companions will misbehave.
The carls are afraid that Derik’s companions will misbehave, but I think it is just harmless grumbling.
The carls are in a bad mood already, and will be displeased to see Derik’s scruffy companions eating us out of house and home.
Derik caused much death; no Chalana Arroy priestesses will help him.
Jaldon’s raids wounded many; all of our neighbors’ Chalana Arroy priestesses will be busy tending to them.
Throughout Dragon Pass, Chalana Arroy priestesses will be busy tending to those wounded by Jaldon’s raids. Still, we can convince one to come to heal the one who slew death’s champion.
The warriors will be furious if we send Derik elsewhere.
The warriors will be glad if we entertain Derik’s companions while he recovers.
If we raid someone while Derik recovers, his thirty worthy companions will help us fight.
Derik was wounded by a manifestation of death; he will not recover.
Magical healing is the only way.
Our magic is strong. We should try to heal him ourselves.
Our magic is weak. There is no point in trying to heal him ourselves.

In the battle between Humakt and Wakboth, the Devil bit the Sword God in half, and cast the pieces aside. This wound would have killed anyone lesser than Humakt, and even he was not able to fight any more that day.
Let us make no more war.
Don’t let those mischievous bulls of his cause any trouble.
Jaldon was an undead monster. We must do all we can for the one who slew him.
It is a good thing Jaldon was not a woman, or Derik would not have beaten him.
Send for priestesses.
We should have done more when he asked us for help.
sceneR239

Derik, now recovered from his wounds, prepares to leave. “I can never thank you properly for all you have done for me. When I was a child, this clan protected me. When my battle with Jaldon made me weaker than a child, you brought me back to health. We go now, down to Prax, where we will take the battle to the nomads. But before we leave, I wish to give you a gift. What shall it be?”
Derik left us, but before he went he offered us a gift.
Ask for a treasure.
We asked for a treasure.
Derik gave us a Hunting Horn, one which would help us find what we sought.
Ask for cattle.
We asked for cattle.

“I have no cattle to give,” Derik said. “But I aim to create a new tribe, the horse people, and we will raid the raiders. When we do so, I will see that some of the spoils are spent to buy you cattle.”
Ask for magic.
We asked for magic.
Magic he gave us.
Ask for silver.
We asked for silver.
Silver he gave us.
“You have given us enough of a gift already, by destroying Jaldon.”
We said, “You have given us enough of a gift already, by destroying Jaldon.”

Tears appeared in the great warrior’s eyes. “Clan of my birth, again you honor me.” He dried his eyes and extemporized a song. He sang it in an unearthly voice, and it was about our clan and his love for us. It was not long before clans throughout Dragon Pass were singing this song. Most of them changed it so that it was about their clans, but they still knew which clan the song was really about.
Cows! Ask for cows!
He is a raider. He has no cows with him.
He is a raider. He has no cows with him. After a while, he may be able to send us some.
Think of silver as an easily-portable cow that does not moo.
A treasure owned by a mighty warrior would help us greatly.
I have heard that Derik is very successful in catching those he chases, even when they hide. Perhaps his treasure would allow us to do the same.
He has already done enough for Dragon Pass, by slaying one of its worst enemies.
He is a great warrior. Maybe he has mighty magic.
By defeating the champion of death, he gained great magic. It would be good if we could get him to share it with us.
Before Orlanth went on the Lightbringers Quest, he called his kings and heroes and priests together. He gave them sacred gifts, and they gifted him with magical tools.
Ask for a treasure; it’s the best deal.
Ask for an elf-smashing treasure.
His blessing alone would edge us closer to the crown.
Cows are the only useful gift.
We need Derik’s war-like, masculine magic, to counteract all of the simpering female magic we get around here.
I told you he’d give us gifts if we treated him right.

Derik Furman, who was born into our clan but now leads his own tribe, has fulfilled his promise, and sent us five milk cows. His thane, Varmath Rhinobane, said we could expect the same next Fire season.
sceneR240
Comfort Derik.
We tried to comfort Derik.
He said, “I will not be comforted until I am a man, and I have brought the raiders low.”
Compose a poem in honor of the slain.
We composed a poem in honor of the slain.
The people praised our poem, which gave them some cheer in a time of mourning.
\x01@N could not properly capture the sorrow of this event, and did not share our poem with the others.
The god-talkers said that the signs were unclear.

The god-talkers said that Derik would grow to be strong and wise. He would leave us, and would become known as a great hero. He would bring death to a deathbringer, laying him under a cairn of skulls. He would found a new people, a nation of outsiders, and would bring honor to the clan.
Sacrifice to the gods for protection from Praxians.
We sacrificed to the gods for protection from Praxians.
The god-talkers said that the signs were unclear. It was hard to know if the gods had heard our entreaties.
The god-talkers said the signs were good. The gods would shield us from desert raiders.
Send a war party to kill Sable Riders.
We sent a war party to kill Sable Riders.
They scoured Dragon Pass for the raiders, but they were not to be found.
They found and battled the desert raiders.
Our fierce warriors shouted the names of the slain as they pulled the nomads from their beasts and cut their throats. We recovered the loot they had pillaged, and more.

Our fierce warriors shouted the names of the slain as they charged the nomads. From atop their peculiar beasts, the raiders slashed at our fighters, wounding some. They fled, and we could not give proper chase to them.
We are too poor to sacrifice.
We can afford to sacrifice.
The Sable Riders are our friends. How could they do this to us?
Sable Riders are tough opponents, who strike and run. The leader of the war party must be a good hunter, as well as a good fighter.
Send our best hunter and six weaponthanes to kill Sable Riders.
We must comfort Derik by burying him in a mound of earth for sixteen days.
Revenge.
The people are disheartened. We must do something to cheer them up.
The people are disheartened. We must do something to cheer them up. We should try a poem, for a failed poem doesn’t carry the consequences of a failed raid.
We should sacrifice.
It is a good time to sacrifice, or conduct a divination.
It is a bad time to sacrifice, or conduct a divination.
Our ancestors cry for blood!
The carls feel sad for Derik, but let’s not get carried away. We still have to plant the crops.
The carls feel sad for Derik, but let’s not get carried away. We still have to harvest the crops.
Derik will achieve his vengeance, and become a great hero in doing so.
The Praxians, led by death’s champion, Jaldon Goldentooth, helped start the Dragonkill War. Jaldon brought 100,000 warriors from Prax to destroy the dragonewt nesting places.
Comfort him.
Kill Sable Riders!
Praxians are enemies of the dragonewts, and so must die!
Vengeance brings nothing but more vengeance.
A family traveling without protection? They were doomed.
Our sacrifices would be stronger if our temples were better.
Elmal, the Defender, will grant us strength.
Track them, kill them.
Derik the Praxian-Hater
sceneR241
Derik, whose family was slain by Sable Riders, became a singleminded young warrior, unpopular with the older \x01@\x17s.
Praise Derik’s pride and stubbornness.
We praised Derik’s pride and stubbornness.
The other \x01@\x17s realized that what they saw as Derik’s faults were in fact his virtues.
The \x01@\x17s grumbled.
Scold Derik for his pride and stubbornness.
We scolded Derik for his pride and stubbornness.
Derik said he would try to be more like us from now on. The other \x01@\x17s thought they would be happy to see him humbled, but instead they were ashamed, and blamed us for scolding him.
Derik laughed grimly, and said, “Do not trouble yourselves with me, for I will not be with you much longer.” The \x01@\x17s were offended by his impertinence.
Send Derik on a raid against Sable Riders.
We sent Derik on a raid against Sable Riders.
How many warriors accompany him?
Tell the \x01@\x17s to let him be.
We told the \x01@\x17s to let him be.
They remembered that pride is an Orlanthi virtue, and not a fault. They promised to cease their grumbling, and look to Derik as a model of good behavior.
We reminded them that pride is an Orlanthi virtue, and not a fault. We discovered that the warriors were unhappy about many other things; their true quarrels were with the clan ring.
Derik’s behavior has offended everyone!
The complaints of the \x01@\x17s are not serious.
The \x01@\x17s are really upset about other things.
Derik does not display the proper virtues of humility and obedience.
Pride is an Orlanthi virtue.
Derik is young, but he is determined. He is ready to lead.
Derik is young, but determined and skillful. He is ready to lead; his hatred of the Sable Riders will assure success.
The \x01@\x17s are forgetting what it is like to be young. Also, they lack Derik’s passion for vengeance.
Why are we troubling ourselves with \x01@\x17 squabbles during Sea season?
Why are we troubling ourselves with \x01@\x17 squabbles during Earth season?
After his initiation, Orlanth was not content with the way that things were. He felt he too deserved a part of the leadership of the world, but his desires were refused by the Emperor.
His hatred is like a disease inside him.
It is good to see a fine young bull testing himself and others.
Condemn his pride and stubbornness! Next thing you know, young Orlanthi will become rebellious and violent!
He must stop and learn to read. That will teach him wisdom.
Fuelled by hate-heat, his heart-fires burn.
The other clans will not make a tribe with us if we are known for indulging troublemakers.
Let him prove himself on a daring raid!
We look at what has happened, and afterwards we say it was destiny.
Derik is back, triumphant. He led our warriors to a Sable Rider encampment, where he slew many and pillaged their goods. None of our warriors were so much as scratched in the fight.
Derik is back, elated. He and our
warriors snuck up on a Sable Rider encampment
warrior snuck up on a Sable Rider encampment

and caused much mischief before sneaking away again. They cut the traces on the Sable Riders’ mounts, and scattered their herd animals. They punched holes in waterskins and loosened every knot they could find. No one saw them, and they managed to steal a few goods while they were there.
sceneR242

Derik Single-Path, who has distinguished himself in many raids, comes before the clan ring and says that he is leaving. “I thank you for raising me and making me a good Orlanthi. Now I must move on, for I have become as strong as I can among a clan of Dragon Pass. I must go out into the world and find new tests for myself, so I can strengthen my powers against the misbegotten raiders of Prax. I ask now for your blessing, before I go.”
Derik Single-Path told us he was leaving to seek new challenges.
Give Derik a parting gift.
We gave him a parting gift.
What do you give him?
He thanked us for our generosity. “Perhaps one day we will meet again,” he said.
Give him permission to leave.
We gave him permission to leave.
“Perhaps one day we will meet again,” he said.
Persuade him to stay.
We tried to convince him to stay.

“I am flattered that you want me to remain,” he said, “but the name you have given me, Single-Path, tells the story. I have a different path to walk than the rest of you. Perhaps, one day, that path will cross yours again.” Then he took his leave of us.
Sacrifice to the gods to protect Derik on his travels.
We sacrificed to the gods to protect Derik on his travels.

He thanked us for our generosity. “The things I will do, I will do not only for vengeance, but to honor you and honor our gods,” he said. “Perhaps one day we will meet again, and I will have accomplishments to share with you.”
Give him a parting magical blessing.
We gave him a parting magical blessing.
How great a blessing?
A token blessing.
A small blessing.
A generous blessing.
All of your clan magic.

He thanked us for our generosity. “Your blessings will aid me in my journey. It will be a long one, because I do not know exactly what I am looking for. Perhaps, after I find it, I will come back here and tell you what it was.” Then he took his leave of us.
He is going away. We’ll never see any benefit from the gifts we give him.
Although we’ll never see any benefit from the gifts we give him, we’re rich enough to make the gesture anyway.
He wants to stay, and forget this silly crusade against the nomads.
It will be hard to convince him to stay. He knows his destiny is elsewhere.
It will be impossible to convince him to stay. He knows his destiny is elsewhere.
A lone traveler faces many dangers in untamed Dragon Pass.
Although he is headstrong and not always obedient, the people have come to love his pride and fervor. The more generous we are with him, the happier they will be.
He will need powerful magic to achieve his lofty goals.
If we sacrifice to the gods, they will protect Derik and bless us at the same time.
When Orlanth began his great journey, many friends came to see him off, wishing him well and giving him their prayers and hopes.
Like a troll coin, he’ll be back.
I wish I was going with him!
He should seek the help of the dragonewts, who ate many foul Praxians during the Dragonkill War.
He will need Ernalda’s protection.
I wish people called me “Single-Path”…
He was never meant to be a farmer.
We’re losing a good weaponthane, no sense increasing our losses.
He has been called to the Hero’s Path. We should be proud of him.
If his family had not died when he was so young, Derik might have chosen a path of peace.
sceneR243

A strange malady grips several of your weaponthanes. Each is suddenly stricken with a fit of palsy, causing them to drop their swords or other heavy items. The fits arrive with no warning, and last for anywhere from a few minutes to several hours. Some of the weaponthanes think that they are brought on by strenuous exercise; the malady most often strikes those sparring on your clan’s training ground.

A strange malady grips several of your warriors. Each is suddenly stricken with a fit of palsy, causing them to drop their swords or other heavy items. The fits arrive with no warning, and last for anywhere from a few minutes to several hours. Some of the warriors think that they are brought on by strenuous exercise; the malady most often strikes those sparring on your clan’s training ground.
Our warriors were stricken by a strange palsy.
The god-talkers said that the malady was caused by
Malia, goddess of disease.
angry ghosts.
It could be cured by \x02\x05propitiating Malia/hiring other shamans/sacrificing to Chalana Arroy/using trickster magic/waiting\x02.
Propitiate Malia.
We propitiated Malia.
