Find shamans to awaken the spirits of the stones.
We decided to find shamans to awaken the stone spirits.
\x01@N finds shamans willing to help us, if you offer them \x01A$ cows.
\x01@N found shamans willing to help us, if we gave them \x01A$ cows.
Forget it.
We thought their price too steep, and did not pursue the matter further.
We could not meet their price of \x01A$ cows, and so did not pursue the matter further.
No shamans were willing to help us.
None were willing to help us.
To be safe, we let the stones alone, and told our hunters to stay away from them.
They awakened the spirits, but then realized that they meant us no good. They predicted ill fortune for many seasons to come.
They awakened the spirits, who said that they would teach us many forgotten secrets of crafting, which would increase our success in trade.
I can find us some shamans.
There are shamans among the \x01@! clan, which is part of our tribe. They will help us.
The shamans will want a gift of ten cows to awaken the stone spirits.
We don’t know who left these stones here.
This area was last inhabited by dragonfriends. If they left these stones, the spirits might be malign.
This area was last inhabited by other dragonfriends. Spirits in the stones might be friendly.
The other clans must hear of this.
If we can boast as well as Orlanth, the other clans will be impressed by our find. If we boast like Eurmal, they will think less of us.
I have heard Orlanth speak in the Sacred Time and understand how to impress our neighbors with glorious words.
The way to protect ourselves from these malign spirits is to dig up the stones.
We should not do anything without knowing more about the spirits sleeping in the stones.
If we dig up the stones, the spirits inside could curse us.
The spirits will be unfriendly towards us. Best to let them slumber.
The spirits will grant us a great boon if we awaken them.
Almost anything that is holy has its own spirit. Not all spirits are friendly.
Dig those rocks!
The spirits won’t like us.
If one of us is to become king one day, we must tell others of this blessing.
Whatever the women think we should do is wrong.
sceneR413

As your people explore your tula, you find many unusual features. One of these is a cave. The cave is inhabited by large, armored rodents with huge mouths filled with teeth, each as sharp as a needle. The creatures swarm out of the cave and attack the carls who found the cave, injuring several of them. The people are worried that these creatures will cause more harm.
We found a cave full of dangerous, armored rodents on our tula.
The dangerous rodents are back.
They found ways out of their cave, even though you blocked it up.
The trickster magic you used against them lured them away, but did not prevent them from returning.
The outsiders you hired to exterminate them didn’t do a very thorough job.
Your weaponthanes thought that they’d killed them all, but here they are again. A few of them must have survived and multiplied.

They swarm to attack several of your horses, mauling one so badly that it must be destroyed. They also bite some of the old women and children. The people say that it is about time the clan ring did something about these loathsome creatures.
The dangerous rodents came back and bit children and horses.
Block the cave entrance.
We blocked up the cave entrance.
Many of the carls were bitten as they piled rocks inside it. They said the warriors should have been ordered to exterminate the creatures.
Have \x01@t lure them away with trickster magic.
\x01@t said \x06 would lure them away with trickster magic.

\x05 pranced about the cave mouth, singing a song which \x06 said was an irresistibly salacious tune in the language of the killer rodents. It seemed absurd, but the rodents formed a line and followed \x01@t as \x06 danced away from the borders of our tula and towards those of the \x01@a clan.
Find outsiders to exterminate the creatures.
We decided to seek outsiders to exterminate the creatures.

We found weaponthanes of the \x01@! clan willing to do it, for half a cow worth of silver each. Many of them were wounded, and they blamed us for not warning them how dangerous these rodents were. They said that all of the creatures were dead.
Order your weaponthanes to exterminate the creatures.
We ordered our weaponthanes to exterminate them.
They said the carls should have been ordered to block the cave entrance.
Many of them were wounded, but they said that they killed them all.
The clan ring did not concern itself with this problem.
The rodents departed.
Don’t worry. They’ll go away of their own accord.
They won’t be easily dealt with.
These things are called Rubble Runners. They multiply like mad, are very dangerous, and nearly impossible to get rid of.
See how quickly the Rubble Runners breed, and how \x02\x03tough/resilient/scrappy\x02 they are?
These things are called Rubble Runners. They multiply like mad and are very dangerous. The only way to get rid of them is to kill each and every one of them.
The carls do not want to go near those things again. They say it time for the weaponthanes to kill them.
The carls do not want to go near those things, but since the weaponthanes have tried their best, the carls feel they must make an effort, too.
The carls do not want to go near those things. Some of them were hoping that trickster magic could lure the beasties away.
These things are called Rubble Runners. They multiply like mad and are very dangerous. Only our own weaponthanes can be trusted to kill each and every one of them.
We can play with magic, or stones, while these Rubble Runners breed and breed and breed. Or we can do what we know we must do: kill them all.
The weaponthanes say that this is a matter for the carls to deal with. They are not rat-catchers.
The weaponthanes don’t want to do this work. But they will, if ordered to.
The weaponthanes say that the Rubble Runners are far nastier than they envisioned. They are almost a worthy foe.
Why risk getting bitten ourselves, when we can find someone to do it for us?
Our neighbors are already angry at us for our reckless use of trickster magic. Let us find another way.
These lowly animals will afflict everyone if we don’t get rid of them.
We must do whatever it takes to get rid of these pests before they overrun our steads, regardless of who thinks what.
These lowly animals are extremely dangerous. This isn’t a matter of who likes to do what, or whose job they think it is. It is a matter of our survival.
We need some kind of magic solution to this infestation.
Only trickster magic can end this infestation.
If we had an Eurmal devotee on the ring, we could make use of trickster magic, which can be useful in odd situations like this.
The carls say that this is a killing matter, and thus the responsibility of the weaponthanes.
The carls say that they will do what they can to get rid of these abominations.
The carls don’t care who gets rid of them, as long as they are gone for good.
During the Storm Age, Orlanth the King was never bedevilled by petty problems such as this!
Creatures like this are often companions to spirits of disease.
This matter is beneath the dignity of proud weaponthanes.
No one will want to marry into our clan if we show ourselves incapable of dealing with a few rodents.
“Better to be killed by an axe than by the nibble of a rat.”
“A scythe in one hand, a sword in the other, and arrows in your teeth.”
This is a problem for the men to deal with — lazy sods!
Animals that travel in packs are no better than men who do the same.
Let us show our neighbors that we are rich enough to have others dispose of our dangerous rodents.
Just let me play my little pipe for them! Please! Please!
Want me to charm them right into the cooking pit?
sceneR414

Glendara, a prosperous carl of your clan, comes before you to complain that her prize stallion, Tempest, has been stolen. Although no one saw the theft, Glendara is certain that it was committed by the sons of Rangarda Dark-Eyes, a well-off carl of the \x01@! clan. “Many times has she offered to buy that horse, and many times did I refuse her. It is the most beautiful stallion in all of Dragon Pass, and I would not let her have it. So she has ordered her sons to steal it.”
Glendara, a carl of our clan, said that her prize stallion, Tempest, had been stolen by Rangarda Dark-Eyes of the \x01@! clan.
Launch a legal claim against Rangarda Dark-Eyes.
We launched a legal claim against Rangarda Dark-Eyes.

Rangarda denied that she had anything to do with the disappearance of Glendara’s horse. Her clan leaders seemed to make an honest effort to determine the truth, but ultimately ruled that there was no evidence of wrongdoing on Rangarda’s part.
Glendara was most displeased by this result.
“By Elmal’s balls,” she swore, “I will recover that horse, if it costs me my last breath.”
We took her claim to the moot.
How much wealth do you give to the other clans before the case is judged?

Although she continued to deny it, the other clans ruled that Rangarda Dark-Eyes was responsible for the disappearance of Tempest. They demanded that she produce the stallion, but she said that she could not. So the \x01@! clan was instead ordered to pay compensation to Glendara.
Despite our victory, Glendara later pronounced herself unsatisfied with the conclusion of the case.
The other clans ruled that there was no evidence to link Rangarda Dark-Eyes to Tempest’s disappearance. They ruled against us, and the people were discouraged.
Glendara said that this would not be the end of the matter.
How many warriors do you send to support your case?
Launch a raid against the \x01@! clan.
We raided the \x01@! clan.

Although we bested the \x01@! warriors, we found no trace of the stallion called Tempest. Glendara swore that Rangarda Dark-Eyes had hidden the horse somewhere, and that she would not rest until she recovered it.

Not only did the \x01@! clan defeat us, but we found no trace of the stallion called Tempest. Glendara swore that Rangarda Dark-Eyes had hidden the horse somewhere, and that she would not rest until she recovered it. The weaponthanes complained that they had been led into a losing battle over a single horse, and blamed the clan ring for making Glendara’s business the clan’s business.
Offer her compensation.
The clan ring offered her compensation.
Glendara said, “It is not the trade value of Tempest that concerns me. It is the principle of the thing. By stealing my prize stallion, she has stolen my honor.”
Persuade her to forget the matter.
Members of the clan ring tried to persuade her to forget the matter.
She would not hear of it. “No argument can sway me, while that mangy, dug-dragging she-dog has my Tempest.”
“This is not a matter for the clan.”
Our leaders said, “This is not a matter for the clan.”
Glendara said that she understood their ruling, and would rely on her own family to make things right.
The carls, however, thought that we should have done more to help her.
That bony old nag probably went off and died somewhere.
Tempest was a fine horse indeed, one worth starting a war over.
Tempest was a fine stallion, but he is not worth fighting over.
It is foolish to make war over a single horse. If we lose, the weaponthanes will be resentful.
It would not be smart to fight them now.
We have a strong case.
Without proof, our case is weak.
Without proof, our case is weak. We are not obligated to make this a clan matter.
Although our case is weak, and we are not obligated to make this a clan matter, we could win by outspending them at the tribal moot.
Rangarda Dark-Eyes did want that stallion, but we have no reason to believe that she ordered it stolen.
Rangarda Dark-Eyes did come here many times to offer to buy the stallion; she may well have ordered her boys to steal it.
Rangarda Dark-Eyes did come here many times to offer to buy the stallion, and I am sure she ordered her boys to steal it.
This could cause trouble between our clans.
Let’s not pull farmers away from the critical task of planting to avenge a deed we have no real proof of!
Let’s not pull farmers away from the critical task of bringing in the harvest to avenge a deed we have no real proof of!
Although the other carls admire her wealth and success, Glendara’s family has always held itself at a remove from the rest of our clan.
Glendara is an eccentric. She has always valued horses more than cows.
Let her pursue this affront to honor on her own terms.
Mark my words — a feud between women always results in the death of men.
Glendara has prospered because of her thrift. We would do well to emulate her — and avoid costly raids and lawsuits.
I have never liked Glendara. She is scornful of me when I can’t come up with the right…you know…it’s on the tip of my…
It is good to have a stormy temperament, but Glendara abuses the privilege.
Glendara is not the most polite woman of our clan.
sceneR415
Glendara’s sons and daughter have done what the clan could not do; they have recovered Tempest.
Glendara’s sons and daughter recovered the stolen stallion Tempest.

They found him in a hidden cave on the \x01@! tula, where they fought off the sons of Rangarda Dark-Eyes. One of the defenders, named Norpent Rangardasson, was slain, and another badly hurt. But justice has been served, for Glendara’s prize horse is hers again, and her honor is restored.
The sons and daughter of Glendara recovered the stallion called Tempest, which they found secreted away on the tula of the \x01@! clan. They slew one of Rangarda Dark-Eye’s sons, and wounded another.
Praise Glendara.
Clan leaders praised Glendara.
The people were cheered by their words.
The people were displeased, for they worried that her actions would embroil the clan in a costly feud.
Scold Glendara.
Clan leaders scolded Glendara.
She was unrepentant.
The people were glad to see her chastised, for they worried that her actions would embroil the clan in a costly feud.
The people were offended; they said that Glendara had taken action to protect her honor, as any true Orlanthi should.
The \x01@! ring claims to have had no knowledge of Rangarda’s crime. They offer you ten cows as a token of apology.
Accept their gift, pronounce the matter settled.
We accepted the gift and pronounced the matter settled.
Reject their gift.
We rejected their gift.
They were most affronted, and said that our alliance with them was ended.
They were most affronted, and said that our intentions were to smear their name regardless of truth.
What do you offer them? (The standard wergild for a slain carl is \x01A .)
They accepted the gifts, though they were still feuding with us over other matters.
Still, their chief agreed that the dispute between Glendara and Rangarda Dark-Eyes is not a part of our current feud with them.
They refused to accept them, and angrily escorted us off their tula.
We were hurried off the tula, gifts and all.

They praised us for our generous gesture, and gave us a reciprocal gift equal in value to our own. They said that we should consider the fighting between the families of Glendara and Rangarda as a personal matter, and one which would not interfere with the strong relations between our two clans.
Glendara and her oldest son made a point of parading Tempest around to all the god-talkers’ steads to celebrate their victory.
If Rangarda’s family is proud, they will seek vengeance against Glendara’s family.
They lied to us! We must seek redress!
Glendara was within her rights to do what she did. There is no cause to scold her.
If this continues, we could see our \x01@! friends quickly turn to foes.
We must stop this from turning into a feud. It will be easier to placate our \x01@! friends than to convince strong-willed Glendara she was wrong to do this.
Some of the carls are worried that this will lead to a costly series of reprisals. Others admire her and support what she did.
When the Rain Cauldron was stolen, King Oskul’s carls came to him for aid. He said, “Do what you must, but I have shed enough blood for seven kings, and will kill no more.”
It is good to have Tempest back in the clan again.
This is still not a matter for clan leaders.
It is wrong to kill a man to gain a horse.
Glendara is an example to us all.
We should be worrying about ghosts and zombies, not about trivial matters such as this.
Glendara is going to get us in trouble!
Good for Glendara!
Glendara has often mocked the need to be vigilant against the elves. Now she has gone too far!
This is no occasion for gift-giving.
Glendara’s honor belongs not to the clan, but to her. She has taken action to protect it, and is worthy of praise.
sceneR416

Brodasart, son of the prosperous carl Glendara, has been slain in an ambush. Friends, who were with him when he was attacked, report that the assailants were relatives of Rangarda Dark-Eyes of the \x01@! clan. According to his friends, the killers said to them, “Stand aside, for our quarrel is only with the family that killed our kinsman, not with others of the \x01@" clan.” Everyone remembers the incident in which Rangarda stole Glendara’s prize stallion, and Glendara’s children slew one of Rangarda’s sons while retrieving it.
Brodasart, son of Glendara, was slain by relatives of Rangarda Dark-Eyes of the \x01@! clan.
Compose a poem in honor of Brodasart.
\x01@N composed a poem in honor of Brodasart.
The poem was a beautiful tribute to a brave fighting carl, and everyone said they would remember it always.
It was a good effort, but no one thought that the poem would be remembered past the time of mourning.
Encourage Glendara to swear off vengeance.
Clan leaders encouraged Glendara to swear off vengeance.

She said that she was sick of heart, and would think only of her son until his funerary rites had been completed. Some of the people said that the clan leaders were wrong to discourage Glendara from pursuing her natural rights of vengeance.
The people cheered this victory, and said that a blow had been struck in Brodasart’s memory.
The people regretted this loss, but said that it was good to have struck a blow in Brodasart’s memory.
Sacrifice to the gods in honor of Brodasart.
We sacrificed in honor of Brodasart.
The people were pleased when the god-talkers reported that the sacrifices had been accepted.
The people sympathized with Glendara’s loss, and some wished we had taken up arms for the sake of Brodasart’s memory.
Warn \x01@! leaders that more killing may follow.
We warned \x01@! leaders that more killing might follow.
The carls were once worried that Glendara would start a feud, but Brodasart was a popular fellow, and now they are hungry for vengeance.
By Orlanth’s thundering song, we must raid them!
There is no occasion for which a poem is unsuitable.
Glendara is within her rights to pursue vengeance.
Glendara is within her rights to pursue vengeance. The people will be unhappy if we try to convince her to forswear these rights.
Our formerly good relations with the \x01@! clan are now in danger.
It is at times like this that our thoughts must turn to the gods, who were the first to experience the pangs of loss, and thus laid the way for the rest of us.
The carls want vengeance, but the clan needs its crops planted.
The carls want vengeance, but the clan needs the crops harvested.
The theft of the Rain Cauldron brought great misery to King Oskul’s people. They begged him to pick up his sword again, the one he had used to slay Bad King Urgrain.
It is good when bulls fight, for it makes strong bulls stronger. But it is bad when this fighting endangers the cows.
It is as I said. Womanish pride has led to the spilling of manly blood.
Does this fruitless bloodshed win us any treasure? We should be exploring, instead.
We must attend to our own clan, peacefully if possible, but if that is not enough, then by warlike means.
Glendara’s family has again struck at the \x01@! family headed by Rangarda Dark-Eyes. This time they set a stead on fire, and Rangarda herself was badly burned. She is not expected to live.

Glendara, the prosperous carl of our clan whose horse was once stolen by Rangarda Dark-Eyes of the \x01@! clan, now lies dead. She succumbed to apoplexy earlier today. Perhaps this will end the feud between the two families.

Remember Rangarda Dark-Eyes of the \x01@! clan, who feuded with Glendara over a stolen horse? She survived when Glendara’s family burned her stead, but now she is as dead as Glendara, felled not by fighting but by a coughing disease. The last words on her lips were of Glendara, exulting in the fact that she outlived her rival.
sceneR417

Young boys of the \x01@! clan, not even men yet, come to your tula and attack another young boy with a sword. Fortunately, the victim’s mother, Domasa Glendarasdaughter, is able to separate the boys before any real harm can be done. It turns out that the \x01@! boys are sons of Norpent Rangardasson, who was slain by Domasa and her late brother Brodasart when they recovered the stolen stallion Tempest from Rangarda Dark-Eyes. The boys seek vengeance in their father’s name, even though they are too young to have a right to it.
Furthering a long-festering feud, young boys of the \x01@! clan came here to attack a boy of our clan.
Convince the boys to renounce vengeance.
We told the boys that they should renounce vengeance.
They said they would do so.
Kill the boys.
We killed the boys.
We let them return to their home tula.
People said that the clan leaders should have done something to end the fight between the families of Glendara and Rangarda, now that both women were long dead.
Ransom the boys to the \x01@! clan.
We ransomed the boys back to their clan.
They fetched a handsome price.
We did not get as much for them as \x01@N had hoped.
Take them back to their clan.
We took them back to their clan.
\x01@! leaders said that we had acted honorably, and said that they hoped this would be the end of the fight between the families of Glendara and Rangarda.
They are boys, yet behave as men. We must kill them.
Until they are men, they have no rights of vengeance.
They are not men, and are not yet accountable for their actions.
I could maybe get three cows each for them.
The proper ransom for these boys would be five cows each.
The proper ransom for these boys would be five cows each, but I think I can get more.
This is not the first time this old feud has caused tensions between our clans.
If another generation takes it up, this feud will never end, or so say the carls.
If another generation takes it up, this feud will never end, or so say the carls. They will be unhappy if we do nothing to stop it.
King Oskul was slain not in a glorious battle, like the ones he fought against Bad King Urgrain, but was killed by a rock-throwing boy, in a feud he swore to end.
Vengeance is like a snake swallowing its tail — its end is never in sight.
Orlanth made justice so that disputes could be ended by words as well as swords.
We must squeeze some benefit out of this annoying dispute.
There is nothing we can do, short of killing them — they will grow older and return to fight again.
These boys will be fine warriors some day; perhaps great poems will be written about them.
sceneR418

Robarth, a member of one of your most prosperous families of carls, is attacked by two brothers from the \x01@! clan. His mother, Domasa Glendarasdaughter, looks on helplessly as they skirmish. Robarth is wounded, but manages to slay one of the brothers, Burthalor. This fight is a deadly reiteration of one that occurred about ten years ago, when all three combatants were children. It grows from a long-running feud between the two families, which started when Burthalor’s grandmother stole a fine stallion from Robarth’s.
Convince Burthalor’s family to renounce further vengeance.
Our clan leaders sought to convince Burthalor’s relatives to renounce further vengeance.
What do you offer them in gifts?

When our people heard of this, they complained that we paid more than the proper wergild for Burthalor’s death. They were affronted by this, because they said that Burthalor had attacked Robarth, and brought his doom upon himself.
Burthalor’s brother, Jakolorth, swore that the dispute would now end. “When you first arrived, such a promise was the last thing on my mind, but your eloquent words have convinced me otherwise.”

Burthalor’s brother, Jakolorth, castigated our emissaries as fools, and said that, if we wanted to end the dispute, that we ought to muzzle our own villainous families. He said he would tell his clanmates of our dishonorable approach to him in his moment of grief.
Convince Robarth and his family to renounce further vengeance.
Our clan leaders sought to convince Robarth and his family to renounce further vengeance.
Does the chief offer them gifts?
The people complained that Robarth’s family were being too well-rewarded for making trouble with our neighbors.
Robarth swore he would not take vengeance, so long as there were no further provocations from Burthalor’s family.

Robarth hotly replied that the clan sought to strip him of his rights of vengeance, which was an unjust theft of his freedom. He rallied many hotheads of the clan to support his position, and there was much unrest in the clan hall that night.
Outlaw Robarth, Domasa, and all of their family members.
We outlawed Robarth and his entire family.

The carls were outraged by this decision, and there was great unrest among them for many weeks afterwards. Eight weeks later, we heard from a trader that Robarth and his relatives were heading back to Heortland. We never learned if they returned in safety to the land of the Pharaoh.
Seek aid of \x01@! leaders in ending the feud.
Our clan leaders sought the aid of their \x01@! counterparts in ending the feud.
They said that they would attempt to restrain Burthalor’s relatives, but could make no promises that they would succeed.
They refused to intervene in what they said was a private matter between families.
The carls rolled their eyes. They knew that this matter was far from settled, ring or no ring.
Our clan leaders refrained from involving themselves in this private matter.
Private feuds have a way of becoming clan feuds, just as water has a way of bubbling when placed over a fire.
It will be very hard to convince Burthalor’s relatives to give up now that he is fresh-killed.
Promises made now will not be considered binding later.
We are obligated to do something about this.
This is not a fight between clans, unless we choose to make it so.
If we wish to give gifts to Burthalor’s family, these should not exceed a fair wergild for his death — that is, ten cows.
Outlaw the family.
We should make certain that this does not damage our relations with the \x01@! clan.
This episode of feuding won’t cause a feud with the entire \x01@! clan, but what about the next?
The only way to guarantee a permanent end to the feud is to outlaw Robarth, Domasa, and the entire family. However, the carls would not stand for it.
Vamar Oskulsson waited until the boy who had killed his father was a man. Then he killed the killer with the same stone that felled great Oskul.
It is proper to pursue vengeance. We should interfere with neither family’s right to do so.
Robarth is not at fault here; he merely defended himself from attack. It is Burthalor’s kin who must promise peace, if peace is to be promised.
Orlanth made justice so that talking would come before fighting.
With his Humakt-cross did Robarth become Burthalor’s meat-maker.
There is always another option.
This is my fault. I should have done something to prevent it.
“Do not speak to oafs or sit with apes.”
Domasa Glendarasdaughter, who took part in the feud with Rangarda Dark-Eyes of the \x01@! clan, died in her sleep last night. Perhaps this will finally end the private feud between the two families.
sceneR419
Outlaw Robarth.
We outlawed Robarth.
The carls were unhappy about this decision, but understood why the clan leaders had taken it.
The people judged this necessary, for they feared being drawn into a full-fledged feud with a stronger clan.
No one ever saw the goods again.
Outlaw Robarth and all of his relatives.
The carls were outraged by this decision, which they said was far out of proportion with Robarth’s offense.
The people judged this a harsh but necessary course of action, for they feared being drawn into a full-fledged feud with a stronger clan.
Return the goods.
We returned the goods.
It turned out that Robarth had stolen goods worth eighty cows.
The \x01@! leaders said that we should do more to contain our errant carls.
The \x01@! leaders were so impressed by our action that they declared our feud over, and said that there would now be peace between our clans — so long as we contained our errant carls.
Return the goods and pay additional compensation.
We returned the goods, and paid more besides.
The \x01@! leaders said that we had shown good faith, and that the actions of our errant carl would not be held against us.
Scold Robarth.
Clan leaders scolded Robarth.
Robarth seemed repentant, and the people felt that the clan leaders had acted wisely in chastising him.
Robarth was unrepentant, and said
he did not care if we ended up feuding with the entire \x01@! clan.
The people were most distressed by his words, for a feud with the \x01@! was precisely what they feared.
The people were disturbed by his lack of respect for our chosen leaders.
he did not care if he added fuel to our feud with the \x01@! clan.
For a time, Robarth and his kin became famous for their generosity.
That caravan contained nothing of value.
That caravan contained perhaps fifty cows worth of goods.
That caravan contained perhaps a sixty cows worth of goods.
That caravan contained perhaps seventy worth of goods.
That caravan contained perhaps eighty cows worth of goods.
Those goods rightly belong to Robarth, who risked his life for them.
Robarth did not seek our permission before doing this thing, so we can rightly confiscate the spoils of his errant act.
Vamar Oskulson slew the man who killed his father, and was in turn laid low by that man’s son.
This is a stupid dispute. No one even remembers how it started.
If only we could all read! Then we might learn, from the chronicles, that vengeance is a sword whose hilt cuts as deep as its blade.
They are our tribemates. Snow-haired Robarth must pay for abusing them so!
With the proceeds from Robarth’s robbery, we could build quite a temple.
No one will marry into Robarth’s family, for they know their sons and daughters might be killed in some pointless squabble.
sceneR420
One of our steads was attacked and looted by a party from the \x01@! clan, who were led by a woman named Iristha.
Convince Iristha to end the family dispute.
We tried to convince Iristha to end the family dispute.
She said that, as far as she was concerned, all accounts were fully paid. She would make no more trouble as long as Janara’s family did the same.
Convince Janara to let the matter lie.
Clan leaders told Janara to let the matter lie.
She agreed to do so, although she said she hoped the spirit of her great-grandmother was not watching, for Glendara would never have approved.
She refused to obey the wishes of the ring, and spread many insults and lies about its members. The people were perturbed by her actions.
Ignore the matter.
Clan leaders chose to ignore the matter. The people were unhappy with their decision.
The people were unhappy with the ring’s decision.
Launch a legal claim against the robbers.
We launched a legal claim against the robbers.
Iristha’s clan is in your tribe.
The \x01@! leaders agreed to return the stolen goods, and also to compensate those wounded in the attack.
The \x01@! leaders agreed to return the stolen goods, but would not compensate those wounded in the attack.
They laughed at us and threw stones at our emissaries, wounding several of them. “We are feuding, yet you try to make a legal claim against us?”
We launched a raid against the \x01@! clan.
We recovered most of the goods that had been stolen from us, and a few more besides.
The weaponthanes were discouraged by our defeat at \x01@! hands.
The goods they took belonged to Janara’s family, not to the clan. But we would do well to ask for compensation for the burned steads.
We must raid them.
It would not be smart to raid them now.
We have a good basis for a legal claim against Iristha.
The \x01@! leaders will not want to jeopardize the good relations between our clans by ruling against us.
Our relations with our tribe mates leave much to be desired. They will rule against us if we take this to a moot.
Our relations with our tribe mates are strong. They would rule in our favor, even if we were not so clearly in the right.
Don’t let these family quarrels interfere with getting our crops planted.
Don’t let these family quarrels interfere with getting our crops harvested.
I believe that this dispute began four generations ago, when Iristha’s great-grandmother stole a horse belonging to Janara’s great-grandmother.
I think I remember my grandmother telling me something about … now what was it?
This dispute will continue until one of the families is extinct. There is nothing we can do.
I am sure that Janara will listen to reason, if we approach her properly.
We must respect Janara’s rights, and raid them.
sceneR421
Surprised carls see two ghosts fighting one another on your tula. The people are gravely concerned — this is a terrible omen.
Our carls saw two ghosts fighting one another.
Once again, carls see two ghosts fighting one another on your tula. The people are
concerned — this is a bad omen.
annoyed — they are sick of coming upon these two old wraiths whacking at each other.
Find shamans to chase the ghosts away.
We looked for shamans to chase the ghosts away.

Shamans from the \x01@a clan volunteered to help us. They performed a lengthy ritual. At its end, they said that the ghosts were those of Robarth, of our clan, and Burthalor, of the \x01@! clan. Their families fought while they were alive, and they had been unable to release themselves from this feud in death. The shamans said they sent the spirits on their way, although they are probably doomed to walk the earth forever, locked in furious embrace.

\x01@N found shamans willing to undertake the task, in exchange for \x01A$ cows. They performed a lengthy ritual. At its end, they said that the ghosts were those of Robarth, of our clan, and Burthalor, of the \x01@! clan. Their families fought while they were alive, and they had been unable to release themselves from this feud in death. The shamans said they sent the spirits on their way, although they are probably doomed to walk the earth forever, locked in furious embrace.
\x01@N found no shamans willing to help.
Launch a legal claim against the ghosts.
We launched a legal claim against the ghosts.

\x01@N found that they were the ghosts of Robarth, of our clan, and Burthalor, of the \x01@! clan. Their families fought while they were alive, and they had been unable to release themselves from this feud in death.
\x01@N found that they were the same old ghosts we’d seen before, spirits caught up in fighting, even in death.
The ghosts agreed that they had been unlawfully occupying lands meant for the living, and promised to continue their fight somewhere else.
The spirits contended that they had every right to occupy themselves in death as they had in life, and refused to leave. The people were alarmed, for they did not know when the hauntings would end.
Ignore the apparitions.
We ignored the apparitions, but the people were uneasy about this.
We ignored the apparitions, but the people were unsettled because of this.
We ignored the apparitions, and the people weren’t happy, but they had seen these particular ghosts often enough that they no longer feared them.
Leave an offering to the ghosts.
We left an offering to the ghosts.
They took our offering, and vanished. We never learned who they were.
They took our offering, and vanished.
Sacrifice to the gods for protection from ghosts.
We made an offering to the gods, so that they might protect us from ghosts.
Our prayers were answered, for the ghosts vanished. We never did learn who they were.
Our prayers were answered, for the ghosts vanished.
The ghosts continued to fight on our lands, and the people were discouraged, thinking that we had lost the favor of the gods.
Scold them for frightening their descendants and relatives.
God-talkers from both clans performed a ritual at the gravesite.
They reminded the ghosts that feuds were for the living, and that both clans would fight better without their interference.
They told the ghosts that the fight was over, and said that since our two clan were not feuding, why should they?

Finally, they chided the spirits for scaring the living and for seeking more than their fair share of attention. “We will honor you properly in the Sacred Time, as befits our ancestors,” they said. “Do not be so greedy as to seek our attention with this unseemly show!”
The ritual seemed to calm the ghosts; they were not seen fighting again by us or by the \x01@! clan.
Let me gather the \x01@! clan god-talkers with ours, and put these spirits to rest.
Orlanth’s brother, Kolat, is master of spirits. He is worshipped only by shamans, so it is shamans we should seek.
It is not unheard of to dispose of ghosts by launching legal claims against them.
From the look of the clan insignia those ghosts are wearing, one of them is from our clan, and the other from the \x01@! clan.
Humakt hates the undead, and ghosts are undead. Sacrifice to Humakt, and he will sweep them away with the flat of his sword.
Sacrifice to Eurmal. He will trick the ghosts into going away.
The gods do not want to be bothered with mere ghosts. Leave an offering directly to the spirits, and bribe them into leaving.
Elmal will defend our hearth against bad spirits.
Sacrifice to Urox; he will scour our tula of Chaos.
No one will want to marry into a ghost-haunted clan.
The elves are responsible for this.
Our tula is the most lovely and bountiful in all of Dragon Pass, so it is no wonder that even the dead want to live here.
They are acting like children. Scold them like children.
We have no right to interfere with their freedoms. Even though they are dead, they are still Orlanthi.
I think that it is old Robarth, and the enemy he slew, Burthalor!
Maybe they need to be reminded that they’re dead.
It’s the moment I’ve been warning you about for ages!
sceneR422
Wilkossi, one of the warriors you sent on your exploratory mission, reports on its unfortunate and premature end.

“One of our fellows, Thadart, was taken by the cruel enemies known as Tusk Riders. We fought valiantly to rescue him, but they were fierce, their boarish steeds were fresh, and they knew the terrain better than we. We have heard from our neighbors about the bloodthirsty gods they worship, and know of their murderous habits. Unlucky Thadart is surely dead by now.”
An exploratory mission came home early to report that one of them had been taken by Tusk Riders, and could now be presumed dead.
Compose a funeral poem.
\x01@N composed a poem to celebrate Thadart’s life and mourn his death.
The people were much cheered by it. They said that other clans would now remember Thadart and his deeds.
All agreed that the poem had not captured Thadart’s heroic qualities. They said that its quality made our commemoration of the man’s death seem shabby.
Give gifts to Thadart’s relatives.
The people were cheered by this display of generosity.
Remind the people that danger is a part of life.
\x01@N reminded the people that danger is a part of life.
The people were moved by the wisdom of \x01@N’s oration.
Although they did not say as much, the people found a hollow ring in \x01@N’s words.
Sacrifice to the gods in Thadart’s honor.
We sacrificed in Thadart’s honor.
The god-talkers said that the sacrifice was accepted, but other signs indicated that the ritual was going to fail. No one could say what this meant.
“There will be no funeral until Thadart is proven dead.”
Clan leaders said, “There will be no funeral until Thadart is proven dead.”

The people were heartened, and remembered the words of King Vingkot: “Six times have my enemies thought me dead, and six times have I returned to harry them. Six times have I vanished, and six times have my friends kept my place at table, knowing that I would be back.”
The people shook their heads. It was clear from the grim expression on their faces that they thought the ring members were fooling themselves.
Send a war party to hunt for Thadart.
We sent a war party to hunt for Thadart.
\x01@\x05, who led the party, searched valiantly for him, but there was no trace of Thadart to be found.
Although many Tusk Riders live in the Stinking Forest, others roam Dragon Pass, causing trouble.
Danger is a part of life.
Thadart was one of our most warlike carls. But he knew that exploration was dangerous when he agreed to go.
Thadart was very skilled with weapons. Even though he was not a weaponthane, we should honor him as one.
We should give gifts to Thadart’s relatives.
A poem has more power to stir the heart than an ordinary speech, or even a generous gift.
We should sacrifice in Thadart’s honor.
We should sacrifice in Thadart’s honor, to speed his spirit to the Halls of the Dead.
King Vingkot disappeared many times, and those of weak confidence thought him slain. But each time he came back, hungry and wanting his dinner, having miraculously escaped death.
If only we knew the location of the Tusk Rider lair — then we could courageously risk our lives to recover Thadart’s bones!
We must think of the family.
It would be cruel to give the people false hope.
If more of us knew how to write, we could not only compose poems, but preserve them for the ages.
“Smile while alive, lest your only grin be that of your skull.”
And to think, we were seeking a bride for Thadart. At least there is no fresh widow to choke on her tears.
Generosity is a holy thing; never more so than at times like these.
There is no point in hunting for Thadart; we will try and fail, and further lower the spirits of our warriors.
By Elmal’s fiery locks, we must find him!
sceneR423

A man who looks like a Tusk Rider comes to your tula, as if expecting a welcome. The man claims to be Thadart, the explorer of your clan, who was taken by Tusk Riders and presumed dead. He says that he was tortured by the Tusk Riders, and left to die of exposure on an altar to their terrible god. But the god spared his life, changing his face so that he looked like a Tusk Rider. “Their god meant it as a grim joke, but you are my clan-mates, and I know that you will accept me, even though I am disfigured.”
A man with the face of a Tusk Rider came to our tula and claimed to be Thadart. He said his disfigurement was a grim joke of the Tusk Riders’ god.
Allow him to return.
We allowed him to return.

He was pleased to be welcomed back. “It is shameful to admit, but part of me was afraid that you would reject me, now that I am disfigured.” Some of the people whispered in fear, for they were certain that Thadart was dead, and this was a monstrous impostor.

He defended himself fiercely, wounding several of our weaponthanes before he was finally driven to his knees. It was Wilkossi, who was with Thadart when he was captured, who finally slit the intruder’s throat. “This is for tainting the memory of our brave, dead comrade,” Wilkossi said. The people were dismayed and upset by this bloody scene.
Convince the people that he should be allowed to return.
Our clan leaders sought to convince the people that he should be allowed to return.
\x01@N’s eloquent words persuaded them that this was indeed Thadart returned, and not some terrible monster.
After all, the clan ring had predicted his eventual return.
The people welcomed him back, and there was much rejoicing.
\x01@N’s words did not quell the fears of the people. They would not look beyond the ugliness of his new visage.
Send him away.
He protested, but when it finally became obvious that we would not relent, he hung his head and left. The people said we had done the right thing, for surely he was a monster.
“You may return, but we will be watching you.”
Our clan leaders said, “You may return, but we will be watching you.”

He said, “I expected a better welcome than this, but I will prove to you that I am the same Thadart I was before.” His words did not quell the worries of the people, who were afraid that he would turn out to be a monster.
It’s not Thadart.
I think he is really Thadart.
I am certain that this is Thadart.
I am certain that this is Thadart, and he remains a good Orlanthi. He will not harm us.
If this is really Thadart, we are obligated to allow him to return.
If this is Thadart, we are still permitted to outlaw him. We would not be the first clan to outlaw a person without just cause.
The people are worried that it is not Thadart, but some kind of monster.
The people are worried that it is not Thadart, but some kind of monster. We must either reject him, or allay their fears.
Who knows what terrible magics the Tusk Rider god is capable of?
A Chaos creature slew King Heort’s holder of regalia and thus gained entry to Heort’s encampment, almost killing our great lord.
We cannot risk letting a monster into our tula.
We must be thoughtful, and not act on our feelings alone.
There is no chance of finding a bride for him now.
The Tusk Rider deity is a destructive boar god. We cannot trust that this is really Thadart.
Kill him before he kills us!
We must give him the benefit of the doubt.
“Laugh when your friends laugh, but return a liar’s words with lies of your own.”
If we do not give himself a chance to prove himself, this is not a clan of free men, but a prison.
Kill him, and then kill the other tusk riders!
I think that this is Thadart, but we should send him away anyway, lest his gruesome features distract us from our battle against the undead.
sceneR424

Thadart, the warrior of your clan whose visage was made monstrous by the alien god of the Tusk Riders, comes before the clan ring, demanding redress of a grievance. “I am dishonored in my own clan. I am continually insulted, whispered about, and treated as some kind of outlaw or foreigner. No one will look me in the eye.
On our last raid, no one would turn their backs to me. When I was cut off by the \x01@! weaponthanes, no one came to my aid.
You welcomed me here, but the others have done everything they can to drive me from the home of my birth.
I do not wish to fight those of my own clan, although they dishonor me. I instead demand that you reproach them for their misbehavior, so that they will correct it.”
Thadart, the warrior whose visage was made monstrous by the alien god of the Tusk Riders, said that other members of the clan had dishonored him, and demanded that the clan ring reproach them.
Give him gifts.
The chief gave him gifts.
What do you offer him?
Thadart accepted the gifts, but was clearly unsatisfied. The people in turn complained that we had encouraged a troublemaker.
Persuade him to be more understanding of the others’ fears.
\x01@N said he should be more tolerant of the others’ fears.
Thadart agreed that it was natural for the others to fear him, and said that he would work to disregard their ignorant slights.
Thadart replied, “If I get killed on a raid, because the others are too fearful to support me, my understanding of their fears will be little consolation.” He repeated his demand.
Persuade the people to treat him with greater respect.
\x01@N sought to persuade the people to treat him with greater respect.

They agreed that they had not behaved properly towards Thadart, and promised to mend their ways. Thadart said he had much ale for them to drink, if they would do him the honor of accepting his hospitality. The people drank long into the night, and the matter was settled.
They protested that Thadart had not proven himself; he could still be a monster, waiting for the time to strike. Thadart was angered by their response and departed, never to return.
Reproach the people for dishonoring him.
\x01@N reproached the people for dishonoring him.

They hung their heads in contrition, and said that they had not acted properly. They promised to mend their ways, and Thadart said he had much ale for them to drink, if they would do him the honor of accepting his hospitality. The people drank long into the night, and the matter was settled.

They were most affronted, and said that the ring had overstepped the bounds of their authority by telling free Orlanthi how to act. Thadart, however, said that his honor had been satisfied by this reproach, and would consider the matter settled.
“You are lucky we let you live here at all.”
Clan leaders said to him, “You are lucky we let you live here at all.”
“It is not lucky to live among dishonorable companions,” Thadart retorted. He packed up his goods and departed, never to be seen again.
Gifts will make him happy.
He doesn’t want gifts. He wants a promise of better treatment.
He must be made to understand that the others treat him badly out of fear.
We have the right to reproach our own people.
We can’t make anyone do anything.
If we reproach the others, he will consider his honor satisfied, even if their response is bad.
What this upstart needs is a good scolding!
If we give him gifts, the others will be jealous.
If we can solve this matter while displeasing neither Thadart or the others, we will gain a reputation for wisdom.
He is lucky we let him live here at all.
The people cannot be blamed. They are simply concerned with the security of the clan.
He will leave our clan eventually, no matter what we do. The fear of the others is too strong to permit him to live here in harmony.
He has been touched by a foreign god. His presence contaminates our shrines and temples.
If our warriors are afraid of one another, our next raid is doomed to fail. We must solve this problem.
I told you taking him in would cause problems.
After reconciling Thadart with the weaponthanes, we should launch a raid, to prove their renewed bonds of friendship.

Thadart, the warrior of your clan whose visage was made monstrous by the alien god of the Tusk Riders, comes before the clan ring with a request. “My parents have tried to find a bride for me, but have been rebuffed at every turn, even by our closest allies. I understand that it is difficult to find a woman to marry a man with a face like mine. I do not expect a beautiful bride, or a clever one, or even a kindly one. But I do need a bride, so that I may carry on the sacred line of my ancestors. I implore you to intervene in this matter, and find me a mate.”
Thadart, the warrior with the Tusk Rider face, implored us to find him a bride.
“If you keep bothering us, we will outlaw you.”
The clan ring said, “If you keep bothering us, we will outlaw you.”
Thadart said that he could tell when he was not wanted, and departed from our tula, never to be seen again.
The people, who had cast aside their earlier fear of him, excoriated the ring members for their cruelty and indifference. They said that the ring was not fit to rule them.
The people were glad to see him go. They said his monstrousness was like a cloud hanging over the entire clan.
“If your parents will not perform this duty, it is not a matter for the ring.”
Our clan leaders said, “If your parents will not perform this duty, it is not a matter for the ring.”
Thadart was clearly disappointed, but said nothing.
The people, who had embraced Thadart and his cause, were dissatisfied with this decision.
Promise to find him a bride.
Clan leaders promised to find him a bride.

After long discussions with a number of friendly clans, we found a prospect for him: Kistrald of the \x01@! clan. She was neither lovely nor clever, but when Thadart’s set eyes upon her, both were filled with love.
The people, who had embraced Thadart and his cause, rejoiced. They set about making a wedding celebration that would be remembered in Dragon Pass for generations to come.

Despite long discussions with a number of friendly clans, we found no prospects for him. In approaching them repeatedly, we strained our relations with them. Thadart could not conceal his disappointment.
The people, who had embraced Thadart and his cause, were also despondent.
Try to find him a bride, but promise nothing.
Without making any promises, clan leaders said they would try to find him a bride.

Despite long discussions with a number of friendly clans, we found no prospects for him. In approaching them repeatedly, we strained our relations with them. Thadart said he was disappointed, but not entirely surprised.
“You cannot expect to marry, looking as you do.”
Clan leaders told him, “You cannot expect to marry, looking as you do.”
Thadart said it was the right of any red-blooded Orlanthi male to seek marriage, no matter what he looked like.
The people said that the ring members were cruel to remind poor Thadart of his deformity, which he had suffered while undertaking the clan’s business.
We can easily find some homely, desperate widow or spinster for him.
We have become used to Thadart’s visage, but it is new to our neighbors. It will be hard to find even a homely widow or spinster for him.
It will be hard to find a bride for him, but I think I can do it.
It will be hard to find a bride for him, but I am nonetheless certain that I can do it.
Thadart is still the object of considerable fear and mistrust among our own clan members. There is no need to exert ourselves on his behalf.
Though once feared and mistrusted, Thadart is now popular with the people. They will be unhappy if we do not help him.
Thadart is still the object of considerable fear and mistrust among our own clan members. The people would be glad to see him go.
We are legally obligated to do as he asks.
It is his parents’ job to find a bride; our duty is only to approve the match once it is made.
Although it is up to his parents to pick a bride, clan leaders may step in when a deserving person finds it difficult to find a mate.
The people will be heartened if we promise to find him a bride, no matter what.
Better not to promise, unless we are sure of success.
It is possible that we will offend our allies by asking them for a bride for a fellow so hideous.
Other clans might think him tainted by Chaos.
Orlanth found it difficult to court Ernalda, but not because he was ugly as a pig.
If we disappoint Thadart, he will find a way to die.
Marriage negotiations are also a good time to extract pledges from our allies to launch a sustained campaign against the undead.
Before his face was changed, I thought it would be easy to find a bride for him. But now…

Thadart, the warrior with the Tusk Rider face, died in the last raid. He attacked recklessly, as if trying to get himself killed. Those who knew him said that he was despondent over the ring’s failure to find a bride for him.
The clan mourned the death of Thadart, the warrior with the Tusk Rider face, who fought recklessly in our last battle.
Although the people did not honor him in life, they are now remorseful, for they can see that Thadart never did anything monstrous, and was in fact as good a person as before his face was changed.
The people mourn his death extravagantly. Although they were unkind to him at first, he had long since won them over. They say the ring should have done more to help him.
sceneR426

Thadart and his bride, Kistrald, have had a son. They have named him Palagor. Although Thadart’s pride in his child is great, some of his relatives, and other members of the clan, are gravely concerned. The boy shares Thadart’s Tusk Rider features. It was hoped that Thadart’s curse would not be hereditary, but indeed it is.
A son, Palagor, was born to Thadart and Kistrald. The people were concerned, because Palagor shared his father’s facial deformity.
Outlaw Thadart, Kistrald, and their son.
We outlawed the three of them.

Some people said that this was the only safe thing to do. Others said that it was harsh and unnecessary, and would reflect badly upon us. The three of them were adopted by Kistrald’s birth clan; their new clan leaders said that they would no longer trust us.
We chose to ignore the event, and the people’s muttering subsided, even if their qualms did not.
Forbid Thadart to father any more children.
We forbade Thadart to father any more children.

Although at first disturbed by this order, he eventually agreed that it was unfair to bring more children in the world to face a life of insults and mistrust. “I will pin all of my hopes on Palagor,” he said.
Thadart’s friends, however, were less accepting of the edict of the clan leaders than he was. They loudly suggested that the ring members should be replaced.
Quell the peoples’ fears.
Clan leaders sought to quell the peoples’ fears.
\x01@N’s soothing words made them less apprehensive, and they gave many generous birth gifts to Thadart and Kistrald.

\x01@N’s words were less soothing than \x06 intended them to be. They served only to heighten the apprehensions of the people, who soon convinced themselves that Thadart’s curse would spread to all children born on our tula.
Conduct a ritual to protect Thadart’s future children from this curse.
We conducted a ritual to protect Thadart’s future children from this curse.
Our god-talkers said that they could not be sure, but that they thought the signs were good.
Our god-talkers said that they could not tell whether the curse had been lifted or not. The only way to know for sure was for Thadart and Kistrald to have another baby.
Demand that the people treat them with respect.
Clan leaders demanded that they be treated with respect.
The people promised to do so, no matter what their fears. To show their good intentions, they gave many generous birth gifts to Thadart and Kistrald.
People said that the gods did not regard Thadart highly, or they would not have cursed him so. They said we were foolish to try to change their minds about this terrible omen.
I would hate to lose a carl who fights as well as Thadart.
A ritual has no chance of succeeding.
I find it hard to think of a mythic event which we could ritually reenact in order to lift this curse.
Not only do I find it hard to think of a mythic event which we could ritually reenact in order to lift this curse, but our magic is weak, as well.
Although I find it hard to think of a mythic event which we could ritually reenact in order to lift this curse, our magic is strong.
We should convince the people that there is nothing to fear.
We could outlaw them.
We could outlaw them, but it would be a very harsh measure.
It is somewhat beyond our legal powers, but we could try to forbid him to father any more children.
The people are afraid. We should quell their fears.
We can enhance our reputation for good leadership by acting magnanimously.
Some peoples of Glorantha have suffered curses that have lasted hundreds of years. The trolls, who are cursed to bear only stunted children, come to mind.
If we act like kings, perhaps one day one of us will become a king.
None of the choices are costly, so I have no objection to any of them.
This is a matter for Thadart and his family, not for the clan ring.
“Make boots for none but yourself, or you’ll be kicked when you make a bad one.”
Rely on the mercy of the gods.
I told you the curse would reach down through the generations.
Thadart and Kistrald have had another child. Like the first child, this one has Thadart’s monstrous visage. The people are most distressed.
Thadart and Kistrald have had another child. This one is free of the curse; it does not look like a Tusk Rider. The people are overjoyed that the curse has been lifted.
sceneR427

Patrols spot a massive group of Tusk Riders galloping towards your tula on their giant boar mounts. The people are frightened. Some of them accuse Thadart, the warrior cursed to wear a Tusk Rider’s face, of alerting them to your tula’s location. He scoffs at this accusation. Then he offers to ride out to the Tusk Riders and negotiate with them. “Perhaps I can make some use of this cursed face, and somehow convince them to turn back their assault.”

We were raided by an enormous force of Tusk Riders. Some people blamed Thadart, the warrior with the Tusk Rider face, for betraying us to them. Thadart denied this accusation, and offered to ride out to negotiate with the Tusk Riders.
Immediately charge the incoming raiders.
We immediately charged the incoming raiders.
Thadart fought as gloriously and courageously as any hero in our legends.
His courage on the battlefield shamed those who had mistrusted him. Afterwards, Thadart
and his family
lived with honor and acceptance in our tula.
His inspired death shamed those who had mistrusted him and vindicated his
family and
friends.
Kill Thadart for betraying you to the Tusk Riders.
We killed Thadart for betraying us to the Tusk Riders.
His wife, Kistrald, bitterly denounced us, and said that we had let ourselves be ruled by fear. She was shouted down as we prepared to face the Tusk Rider attack.

After the battle, Thadart’s family went missing. The people were deeply ashamed and saddened, too, when we found that Kistrald had deliberately poisoned herself and her children rather than live among hostile people.
After the battle, we realized that we had unfairly blamed Thadart. His friends said the ring had repaid Thadart’s loyalty with death.
Let Thadart negotiate with the Tusk Riders.
We let him do this.

Our patrollers watched nervously as Thadart rode out. For a moment, it looked as if the tuskers would ride right over him, but then they stopped, and parleyed. We anxiously looked on as Thadart gestured and snorted at the Tusk Rider leaders, and they gestured and snorted in return.
Finally they turned away, and the assault was averted. Thadart returned to us, and everyone asked him how he had convinced them to leave.
Abruptly, one of them took his spear and impaled poor Thadart upon it. They laughed as Thadart died, and then rode on towards us.
Steel yourselves for the attack.
We steeled ourselves for the attack.
Tell Thadart to direct the Tusk Riders to another clan.
We told Thadart to direct the Tusk Riders to another clan.

There once was a time when gods and people walked the earth together. Your clan traces its ancestry back to those times.\n\nYour clan history begins when you joined the forces of the storm god Orlanth. Back then, Orlanth was simply one of many upstart, rebellious gods bent upon conquest of the world. Orlanth’s unique contributions at that time were personal honor, and a close kinship to the other deities who seemed to be on the winning side.

After many tribulations, adventures, and discoveries Orlanth proved himself worthy of marrying Ernalda, the Earth Mother. The two formed the Marriage Ring, and created a great harmony in the world through this sacred bond. Your clan took part in the wedding ceremony. Most clans either whooped with Orlanth, or learned a secret from Ernalda. A few clans stood with Elmal, God of Horses and the Sun, as an honor guard.\n\nHow did you prepare for the great marriage?
Your men and women donned gleaming armor and stood guard with Elmal, to protect the celebrants from Orlanth’s\nmany enemies.
Your men whooped with Orlanth, and drank the Eight Known Drinks, so that your heads would hurt during the ceremony.
Your women withdrew with Ernalda, and learned a List of Names, which they promised not to repeat to the men.

Orlanth’s struggle to remake the world was just beginning, and many other gods joined him in it. Orlanth fought Yelm the Bright Emperor, and undertook many wars of conquest. Other, more peaceful deeds were just as important. Your earliest Famous Event was:
The Healing of Orlanth, when the merciful goddess Chalana Arroy joined Orlanth’s tribe.
The Hundred-Day Hunt, when Orlanth and his son Odayla tracked the Sky Bear.
Jested’s Settlement, where Orlanth and Issaries the Talking God outwitted foreign deities in a difficult negotiation.
The Procession of the Animals, where Uralda\nthe Cow Mother led the sacred herds into\nOrlanth’s stead.
When Barntar, son of Orlanth and Ernalda, learned of harnessing oxen to plow.
When Lhankor Mhy, the Knowing God, learned how to use the marking bone, which could mark signs of power upon anything.
When Pella, the pottery goddess, made the first pot to store grain in.
When Roitina, lady of dance, first did the Clan-making Dance.

Orlanth succeeded in remaking the world. Thus began the golden era called the Storm Age. Orlanth’s son Vingkot was a famous warlord during this time. Most people in the area were his followers. He introduced new principles, such as the rule of hospitality, which said that after you invited people into your steads, you could not attack or harm them. Thus was much treachery banished from Orlanthi society. Many who would not have survived agreed to his new ways in order to gain his protection. He was a great organizer, and helped the many scattered people form into new clans and tribes. Your clan was one of those aided by King Vingkot. After you proved yourselves robust and capable of survival, Vingkot placed a remnant people under your protection. They were the Nalda Bin, or “Stick Farmers.” You had a choice whether to make them into thralls (slaves) or adopt them as members of your clan.\n\nHow did you add these strangers?
As thralls.
As adopted family.
The foes of the Vingkotlings were many, and your people fought hard against them. Which one of them in particular did you fight?
Boztakang the Troll Lord.
Ukkar Gra, King of the Basmoli Beastmen.
Chinkis Mor, the Elf Warlord.
Tada the Green, champion of the flat land\ncalled Prax.
Ves Venna, Warlord of the Ice Tribe.

The Storm Age ended in disaster, when the gods and creatures of Chaos came, and destroyed nearly everything. Orlanth and his allies fought hard, but Chaos almost always won. Many gods died, and new ones rose to prominence. Many people died, too. Catastrophes shook the world: the Sun Fall, the Rain of Blood, and the terrible Laughing Tsunami. The Darkness got so bad that even Orlanth and his companions had to abandon humans to their own destiny. Only a few deities, either small ones or weak ones, remained. The world stagnated and died. Your clan was diminished to a ragged handful of hardy survivors.

Heort the King was the leader who emerged amid the turmoil of the Darkness. The efforts of Heort and his companions helped set the world in order again. He created the laws that we follow to this day. One of the great distinctions which Heort discerned among his clans was that some of them tended towards either peace or war, while others maintained a balance between these two principles.\n\nWhich kind was your clan?
War.
Balanced.
Peace.

Finally, the sun rose again. While the rest of society worked to protect themselves, find food, or otherwise just survive, the First Priests worked to re-establish links with the ancient deities. With a new harmony between people and deities, the world was slowly improved. Once the awakening process had begun, it got easier and went quicker as the gods woke each other, too.\n\nWho was the first deity which your clan help to awaken?
None. Our ancestors are good enough.
~None. We retained worship of our living deity:
Elmal, the Loyal Thane.
Urox, the Storm Bull.
Odayla the Hunter.

Things have been different since the Dawn, thirteen hundred years ago. Orlanth and the other gods retreated from the world, leaving it to mortals. You can still contact them through ritual and sacrifice, or enter their realm by re-enacting stories about their deeds, which contain great magic. But they no longer walk beside you. When you settled in a new place, you marked this great change in the world by naming your land not after a god, but after a mortal like yourselves. You called it Heortland, in honor of the king who taught you how to survive during the Darkness.

About six hundred years ago, a dragon approached you, in either its own form or that of a human with a dragon’s soul inside it. The dragons had always been hostile, or at the very best utterly uncaring. Orlanth was always the dragon-slayer. You had to choose whether to believe it and cooperate and learn to do what dragons know, or whether to maintain neutrality.\n\nWhat was your attitude towards the dragons?
Hostile. We would never believe a dragon.
Neutral. We didn’t go along.
Positive. We joined into their dragon knowledge.

Most of the people who said “Yes” to the dragons moved to Dragon Pass, a land to the north of your home. You stayed in Heortland, and it is a good thing, too, for a little over two hundred years ago, the dragons rose up and ate everyone who lived in Dragon Pass. They ate the Orlanthi along with all of the other foolish human dragonfriends. For a long time, no humans went to Dragon Pass; they were sure that the dragons would eat them, too.

Recent events made you think twice about the abandoned land of Dragon Pass. A generation ago, a usurper who called himself the Pharaoh came to Heortland and started a civil war. Your clan broke into disputes, sometimes violent, about whether to support the Pharaoh. In the end, your group of dissidents decided it would be better to risk the dangers of Dragon Pass than to stay and kill your own kin, the greatest sin an Orlanthi can commit. Those unable to live under the Pharaoh would move northward to Dragon Pass. People of similar beliefs from other clans had already made the same decision, and settled there. So you made a new clan, just as your ancestors had done in the days of King Heort.

Your new clan made the dangerous trek to Dragon Pass and selected a place to live. Like the other Orlanthi refugees from Heortland, you settled in Quiviniland, a mountainous area in the southeast of Dragon Pass. You would call these lands your home, or tula. Tradition required you to make a formal land-claim.\n\nHow much land did you claim?
As much as we needed, no more.
More than we needed, to grow into.
Lots more than we would probably need.
Huge tracts, far more than needed.
